articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Variable Voltage SMPS Device Using Bluetooth Controller for Mode Selection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: This paper introduces an optimized design procedure for a DC-DC buck, boost and buck-boost configurations in single circuit with an integrated dissipative snubber, aiming to enhance performance and efficiency. The conventional buck-boost converter's versatility in adjusting output voltage is complemented by the dissipative snubber, mitigating hard switching challenges in power semiconductors. Utilizing advanced control techniques for seamless transitions between step-down and step-up modes, the proposed circuit ensures optimal operation across varying input voltages. The research delves into the snubber's impact on limiting maximum voltage stress across the switch, considering power losses in the snubber resistor. Simulation and analysis results validate the design's effectiveness in meeting voltage regulation requirements, showcasing its adaptability to diverse electronic applications. This optimized design methodology holds promise for improving DC-DC converter efficiency in practical applications where mitigating switching losses and optimizing voltage stress are critical considerations. Also this proposed converter provides output simultaneously for buck and boost configurations. The mode selection is made using Bluetooth technology.

articleTitle: A Modified Non-Isolated Switched-Inductor based Boost Converter using Voltage Multiplier Cell for EV Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: This paper proposes a compelling approach to DC-DC conversion using a Switched Inductor Boost Converter (SIBC) with a Voltage Multiplier Cell (VMC). The VMC increases voltage gain, allowing the single switch of the SIBC to operate at a lower duty cycle, thus reducing switch voltage stress. Circuit analysis is used to design the converter's passive elements like inductor, capacitors play a crucial role in regulating the energy flow which are used in the converter. A small-signal model is developed to assess converter stability. The paper compares the proposed converter with existing ones, comparison highlights the advantages of the proposed design. MATLAB/Simulink is employed for both implementation and performance analysis.

articleTitle: High Solar Photovoltaic Generation Penetration Effects on Power System Small Signal Stability Using Modal Analysis and Time Domain Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: There is a world of difference between traditional synchronous generators and solar photovoltaic (PV) systems. Power electronic inverters are dynamic devices that lack in-ertia and are controlled by their properties. Gaining a clear understanding of how power system dynamic performance will be affected by the rising penetration of solar PV generation is crucial. Using modal analysis and time-domain modeling, this research takes a look at how solar PV generation affects the stability of power system tiny signals. Based on its location and penetration level, solar PV generation can have either a positive or negative effect on tiny signal stability, according to the simulation results. If the tiny signal stability is negatively impacted by solar PV integration, it may be necessary to keep important synchronous generators online or take other measures to ensure that low-frequency oscillations are adequately dampened.

articleTitle: Indigenous Innovations: Propelling Drones with SYNCREL Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: This research article deals with the modelling and analysis of synchronous reluctance motor for drone applications. A 24 V, 36 A, 6000 RPM synchronous reluctance motor is modelled by using finite element software to investigate its performance characteristics as torque, inductance, magneto motive force (MMF), current pattern, heat distribution, harmonic and frequency. A rated torque of SyRM is 1.25 Nm is derived by modelling using FEA. The machine maximum temperature is estimated as 59 degree Celsius. The structural behavior of the machine is predicted in both tangentially, radially., as 4th, 8<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> and 12th harmonic order. A comparative study is executed among stator and rotor in terms of harmonic amplitude, order and tangential.

articleTitle: PMSM Motors in the Air: Investigating Torque Characteristics for Optimal Drone Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: The PMSM motor has salient features has power density, compact in size, precision control but, this motor suffers from torque ripple, as described in this research article. The comparative investigation among PMSM, PMSM with Circular Flux barriers, PMSM with Tubular Flux barriers and Interior Permanent Magnet are implemented to obtain the parameters as Torque, Cogging Torque, Torque-Speed, and Instantaneous field Distribution. All these machines are modelled and analysed with a common specification as supply voltage of 24V, rated current of 36A and rated speed of 6000RPM. From the above comparison, it is evident that the PMSM is superior among other motors and suits for drone applications.

articleTitle: Enhancing Reliability and Performance of Hybrid (PV and SEGP) Energy Island Microgrid Systems for Community Modernization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: In response to escalating energy demand and environmental concerns, renewable energy sources have emerged as crucial alternatives to conventional power generation. This paper proposes an innovative solution to address reliability and performance challenges in renewable hybrid PV and Sustainable Energy Generating Pad (SEGP) energy systems by integrating power electronics devices connected to the AC-DC microgrid system. The study uses ETAP software for simulation to identify Busbar instability and the system's performance. Subsequent adjustments to the power electronics devices result in notable system reliability and performance enhancements of about 98-100%, leading to reduced power losses. These findings underscore the transformative potential of this approach in bolstering societal sustainability by sustaining renewable electricity generation and mitigating environmental impacts. The research significantly contributes to ongoing efforts to bridge the gap between energy supply and demand for stable island mode microgrid operation mechanisms, addressing challenges associated with renewable energy generation with alternative energy source methods.

articleTitle: Implementation of a Wireless Energy Monitoring and Databasing System Using PLC
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: With the transition of industries to automation, Programmable Logic Controllers (PLCs) have become a central unit for control engineering. Industries have also started using Energy Monitoring systems seeking to identify operational trends and irregular spikes. This paper discusses the implementation of a wireless Energy Monitoring and Databasing system using a PLC as its central unit. Acknowledging the prevalent trend of incorporating additional controllers such as the Raspberry Pi for the implementation of Energy Monitoring systems, this research seeks to further the paradigm by leveraging the inherent capabilities of a PLC. The proposed system uses the Select MFM 383a, with RS 485, a Siemens 1215 Controller, MQTT, and AWS Cloud services. The results show that the PLC is able to perform this task highlighting its suitability for this application in industrial settings.

articleTitle: Design and Control of Electric Vehicle Charger Using Bi-Directional DC-DC CUK Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: This paper proposes an innovative approach to the design and control of Electric Vehicle Chargers (EVCs) by employing a DC-DC CUK converter. The surge in Electric Vehicle (EV) adoption necessitates efficient, reliable and grid-compatible charging infrastructure. To address this demand, a comprehensive study focused on optimizing the CUK converter for EVCs is described in this paper. This approach includes meticulous component selection, topology configuration, and advanced control algorithms to achieve superior voltage regulation and enhanced efficiency. Further, the challenges posed by input voltage variations and dynamic load fluctuations commonly encountered in EV charging scenarios is also analyzed to ensure stable and reliable operation of the EVCs. The simulation results suggest that the proposed system is feasible and practical, with higher charging efficiency and lower power losses. Additionally, this approach also enhances grid integration capabilities, aligning with the sustainability goals of modern transportation systems. In summary, review of the literature and detailed simulation on bidirectional DC-DC CUK converters has been conducted about their modes of operation. MATLAB SIMULINK software has been utilized to simulate the Steady State Analysis.

articleTitle: Estimation of State of Charge and State of Health in Aged Lithium-Ion Battery Performance: An Extended Kalman Filter Approach for Predictive Modelling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: This study emphasizes the increasing significanceof lithium-ion technology in both consumer devices and electriccars, citing characteristics such as high energy density, longevity, and lack of memory effect. In this setting, it is critical to accurately determine factors such as state of charge (SoC) and State of Health to develop precise battery models. The study describes an improved algorithm for predicting SoC in cylindrical lithium cells, using MATLAB/Simulink and experimental data. A second-order mathematical model. Thevenin circuit was designed to replicate battery operation and the Lookup Table method in Simulink is used to identify internal parameters. The major goal is to improve the accuracy of SoC and SoH estimates by approximating the most accurate values of internal parameters using the Extended KalmanFilter(EKF) algorithm's advantages. This paper advances the understanding and efficiency of lithium-ion battery systems in various applications.

articleTitle: Wind Speed Prediction Using Fuzzy C Means Clustering with LSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: This paper presents a clustering approach before long short-term memory (LSTM) modeling for preprocessing to enhance the model's predictability without increasing the complexity of the LSTM model. Relevant features are selected, and principal component analysis (PCA) is performed before clustering to focus on the main features in the data. The results of the clustering, including cluster centres for each principal component and membership, are then given to the LSTM for model training. The performance of fuzzy C-means in integration with long short-term memory (FCM-LSTM) model is compared with other deep learning models in terms of performance metrics. The superior performance of the proposed model is visualized through prediction graphs and performance metrics. Thus, using an unsupervised method like clustering before modeling provides an advantage in detecting anomalies or hidden patterns in wind data.

articleTitle: Wind Power Integrated AC Microgrid Based Frequency Controller
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: The microgrids have a mixed structure with synchronous machine equivalence and multiple DGs connected via inverters. The presence of inverters is reflected in terms of deficiency in AC microgrid inertia. As a result, deficiency in grid inertia reflects in terms of large change in frequency, fast change rate of grid states. However, linear quadratic regulator (LQR) based control law is designed to maintain nominal grid frequency at lowest level against electronics devices based DGs interface. The basic objective of this study is to reduce states sensitivity towards inertia variations in AC microgrid. The designed law is optimized through linear matrix inequality (LMI). The simulations are implemented in MATLAB. The presented LQR is designed to minimize deviations in state trajectories with improved stability against load and wind random and unwanted sudden changes. The simulated trajectories showcase the robustness of the presented control scheme in achieving minimum time characteristics.

articleTitle: Enhancing Electric Vehicle Charging Stations with Renewable Energy Integration through Advanced Control Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: This paper presents a novel microgrid model for EV charging stations, primarily powered by renewable energy sources such as solar photovoltaics (PV) and wind. The proposed model employs an advanced control algorithm to independently manage solar PV, wind turbines, battery storage, and the EV charging process, intricately coordinated with the AC grids. A key innovation of our model is the optimization of on-grid charging through the strategic selection of component ratings for PV and wind converters. This optimization is achieved using a Fuzzy Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) controller enhanced by Grey Wolf Optimization, ensuring maximal energy extraction from renewable sources. Furthermore, the model innovatively incorporates Q Learning algorithms to repurpose the braking torque energy of EVs back into the battery charging circuit. Empirical results demonstrate the superiority of the proposed model over existing methods. Notably, it exhibits a 15.5 % improvement in energy efficiency and an 8.3 % reduction in overall operational costs.

articleTitle: Analysis of Various Machine Learning Approaches for Predicting Sun Irradiation Levels
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: The present paper examines how well various machine learning approaches predict solar irradiation levels. Applications like solar energy generation and climate modeling rely on accurate predictions of sun irradiation. Several machine learning approaches, such as Gaussian Process Regression (GPR), Artificial Neural Network (ANN), Decision Tree (DT), Linear Regression (LR), and Support Vector Machine (SVM), are investigated and compared in the present study. The investigation entails comparing the approaches' predicted accuracy and assessing their effectiveness using historical data on solar irradiation for the Dehradun region of India (30°19'27.95"N, 78°2'2.11 “E). Also, this shows how well each method scales and how efficient it is computationally, with reference to the lower error in sun irradiance prediction, especially for the GPR technique, as the root mean square error (0.797098637), mean square error (0.635366237), mean absolute error (0.430421925), and regression value (0.999992228).

articleTitle: Switching Study of Twin Two-Level Seven Phase Voltage Source Inverter System for Multi-Level Outcome
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: - Various industrial high-power applications, such as electric boats, hybrid cars, and ship propulsion, use multilevel inverters. However, as the number of levels rises, so does the complexity of multilevel inverters, which has certain drawbacks. Some of the drawbacks of multilevel inverters can be solved by a dual two-level inverter system. The author of this article uses a two different switching of space vector pulse width modulation (SVPWM) technique to suggest a multi-level outcome for a twin two-level 7-phase voltage source inverter (VSI) system. This kind of research has never been done before. The total harmonic distortion (THD) and basic component performance of the system were investigated using simulation findings. To back up the conclusions, simulation data have been presented.

articleTitle: Effects of Airgap Non-Uniformity on Performance and Reliability of Induction Motors for Special Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: Induction motors (IM) are more economical, robust, and reliable compared to rare-earth-based machines and hence continue to dominate the market share, especially for industrial applications. However, the rotor eccentricity fault is one of the weak links in the IM reliability chain. This paper presents a detailed magnetic field transient analysis of canned induction motors for simulating static and dynamic eccentricity faults. In the present work, a detailed FEA study was carried out to investigate the effect of rotor eccentricity on important performance parameters of an induction motor such as torque, current, and air gap flux density. The effect of increasing eccentricity on the unbalanced magnetic pull is also studied for static and dynamic eccentricity.

articleTitle: A Network-Aware Aggregation and Control Framework for Residential Distributed Energy Resources
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: This paper introduces a framework designed to address the challenges posed by numerous small-capacity distributed energy resources (DERs), which significantly complicate management for distribution system operators. The framework focuses on aggregating and controlling small-scale residential DERs while adhering to distribution network constraints. It establishes coordination among utility operators, community aggregators, and residential prosumers. Each entity evaluates the flexibility of DERs within its operational domain, deter-mining feasible flexibility levels. With this information, optimal dispatch setpoints for DERs are computed to support prosumer preferences, regulate node voltages, and provide cost-optimal operations. Numerical simulations conducted on a segment of an IEEE-123 bus radial distribution network illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in mitigating voltage issues and supporting cost-ontimal operation.

articleTitle: Solution of Optimal Power Flow Problems Using Enhanced Hunter Pray Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: This work presents a new algorithm specifically developed to solve the Optimal Active Power Dispatch (OAPD) problems. The OAPD problem aims to minimize total voltage deviation, quadratic fuel cost, and complex nonlinear fuel cost, while considering the impact of valve point loading (VPL) effects and prohibited operating zone (POZ). This is done to maintain an economically efficient operational condition in a power system. The proposed hybrid algorithm combines the non-uniform mutation process with the Hunter-Prey Optimization Algorithm (HPOA) in order to improve the local search capabilities of HPOA. HPOA manages the global search process, whereas non-uniform mutation process and HPOA operate together for local search process. This combined technique effectively addresses complex nonlinear optimization problems. The proposed method is applied to determine the optimal settings to minimize real power loss, simple quadratic fuel cost and the fuel cost with VPL and POZ. The IEEE 30 bus system is used to evaluate the algorithm that is being considered. After that, its results are compared to those of other published algorithms.

articleTitle: Frequency Control of Power System Under Denial of Service Attack
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: Power grids that integrate cyber-physical systems are vulnerable to a variety of cyberthreats, such as DoS assaults, which can impair system stability and interfere with LFC operations. The proposed study suggests a unique method for improving Load Frequency Control (LFC) of power systems by use of distributed controllers optimized by Subtraction Average Based Optimization (SABO). Through extensive simulation studies on a benchmark power system model under different DoS attack scenarios, the effectiveness of the proposed approach in mitigating the impact of cyber-attacks on LFC performance is evaluated. Results demonstrate improved system stability by taking into account the Integral Squared Error (ISE), reduced frequency deviations, and enhanced resilience compared to traditional control methods. The SABO-optimized distributed controllers offer a promising solution for strengthening power grid resilience against DoS attacks, thereby safeguarding critical infrastructure and maintaining uninterrupted electricity supply.

articleTitle: Automatic Phase Sequence Detection in BLDC Motor Drives with Hall Sensors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: Brushless DC (BLDC) motors with hall effect sensors are one of the most common arrangements in electric vehicle drives, particularly in E-rickshaw type of applications. The drive operation is dependent on the hall sensor signals that correspond to particular rotor position in an electrical cycle. Each hall is placed in fixed spatial configuration against the three phase stator windings. Thus, hall signal pattern is fixed against fixed motor phase sequence in clockwise or counterclockwise rotation. This sequence locking is necessary for the drive operation. If correct sequencing is not used for connecting motor phase or hall terminals with controller terminals, the phase sequence detected by the controller is different from the actual sequence. The switching pattern implemented by the controller is incorrect in such a case. This paper presents a scheme for automatic phase detection and subsequent correction in controller without requiring physical reconnection of motor phase windings.

articleTitle: Reliability analysis of VRLA Batteries Using Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA) Technique for hot and Semi-Arid Indian Climatic Condition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: The reliability of valve-regulated lead acid batteries has been one of the major areas of concern for use in storage applications alongside solar rooftop plants. This work for the first time, addresses the implementation of FMEA for one valve-regulated lead acid battery bank to study the reliability of VRLA batteries. The battery parts in which failures are observed are terminals, Surface, cables, safety vents; non-invasive testing of terminal voltage, battery temperature, capacity degradation and visual inspection was performed. It is found that the failure modes associated with the maximum risk level for the battery bank under investigation are battery dry-out having the highest value of RPN (RPN=360) and battery surface bulging (RPN=280) due to improper ventilation and high ambient (room) temperatures. The risks associated with these failure modes can be addressed by timely prediction and prevention of each failure mode.

articleTitle: An Enhancement Mode Double T- Gate Field Plate GaN HEMT for Power Electronics Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: In this report, we have proposed and investigated p-GaN HEMT for improved performance. The proposed device utilises a double T-field plate at the gate electrode of the proposed device to reduce electric field near the drain edge of the gate. The reduction in electric field enhances the breakdown voltage (BV) of the proposed device which is suitable for high power electronics application. The simulation findings were validated by calibrating the device models with experimental results. Also, the study includes a comparative analysis exhibiting superior DC characteristics, such as enhanced on-current, maximum drain current, high BV, low gate leakage current and elevated transconductance in contrast to conventional T-Field plate HEMTs. Moreover, the fabrication process for our device has been outlined, accompanied by optimization efforts aimed to achieving peak performance, particularly focusing on BV. Additionally, a comparative analysis with existing state-of-the-art devices has been conducted to evaluate the superiority of our device.

articleTitle: Comparison of Control Strategies PI, FOPID, and ANFIS Controllers in EV System for Microgrid Interactive System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: Plug-in electric vehicles (PEVs) interact with AC power grid the bidirectional nature, Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) and Grid-to-Vehicle (G2V) operations effectively. In this article, a buck- boost converter integrated in non-isolated Bi-Directional with adaptive control in regard to reference values is presented as an efficient way to manage EV batteries charging and discharging. A comparison analysis of PI, FOPID and ANFIS was carried out during this research. The PI, FOPID, and ANFIS controllers were simulated in a single-phase network with on-board EV charger in MATLAB/Simulink. The comparison study unequivocally shows that ANFIS-based controllers are more effective than FOPID and PI controllers.

articleTitle: Bayesian Optimized LSBoost Model for the DC Fault Location in a MT-VSC-HVDC Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: The proliferation of direct current (DC) networks within utility systems presents novel challenges for fault localization., distinct from traditional AC grids. Unlike AC systems., DC grids exhibit unique transient behaviors., rendering conventional fault restoration techniques less effective. Precise fault localization is crucial for minimizing costs and ensuring swift power restoration in DC networks., particularly in multi-terminal high-voltage direct current systems utilizing voltage source converters. This study proposes a novel approach for identifying high-resistance grounding defects in HVDC transmission lines., a task known for its complexity. By leveraging Bayesian optimization., we develop a tailored Least Squares Boosting model optimized for DC fault localization in MT - HVDC systems. Extensive experimentation demonstrates our method’ s efficacy., achieving a Mean Squared Error (MSE) of 0.1784 and Root-MSE of 0.4224. These results signify improved accuracy and efficiency in fault localization., contributing to the reliability and robustness of DC grid operations., and facilitating effective maintenance and restoration strategies.

articleTitle: Three-Port DC-DC Converter with Galvanic Isolation Using Multi-Winding Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: A three port DC-DC converter that employs push-pull topology with isolation is presented. The converter transfers power from two DC input sources using a multi-winding transformer to the load. The high gain of the converter is achieved using quasi - switched boost (qSB) network, switched capacitor (SC) topology, multi winding transformer turn's ratio and voltage doubler circuit (VDR). The converter operation, steady state analysis deriving output voltage and comparison with similar topologies are presented. MATLAB/ Simulink results justify the converter operation and analysis. The underlined features of proposed converter are (i) high voltage conversion ratio (ii) galvanic isolation (iii) reduced utilization of semiconductor devices and (iv) capability to combine multiple input sources.

articleTitle: Analysis and Simulation of Charging/Discharging of Lithium-Ion Battery in Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: The increasing adoption of EVs as a sustainable transportation solution has arisen the need of research on performance enhancement of energy storage technologies. Li-Ion batteries play a critical role in driving the widespread acceptance of EV systems. Li-Ion batteries need protection to control overcharged /undercharged condition which improves the life span and efficiency of the battery. Therefore, a suitable control method is needed to improve the protection of the battery. The objective of the paper is to analyse the performance of Li-Ion batteries energy management system by monitoring and balancing the cell voltage. Four control methods are used: Discharging Method using MOSFET, Constant Current method, Constant Voltage method and Constant Current Constant Voltage method. The control strategies on Li-Ion battery banks are implemented using MATLAB Simulink. The CCCV method demonstrates proficient control over battery charging, facilitating a smooth transition from Constant Current to Constant Voltage to prevent overcharging.

articleTitle: GACNNXAI: Employing Genetic Algorithm-Enhanced Convolutional Neural Networks and Explainable Artificial Intelligence and its Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: We have proposed a Genetic Algorithm Enhanced Convolutional Neural Network coupled with Explainable Artificial Intelligence for oral cancer detection in medical imaging. Our approach associated CNN with an explanation method to make CNN-based diagnostic decisions more understandable for a clinician. A high resolution of oral imaging is a challenge due to downsampling in several CNN networks. By optimizing the hyperparameters of CNN using Genetic Algorithms, we compensated for downsampling. Our model's hyperparameters, such as the number of layers, filter size, and learning rate, were adjusted based on performance in the validation set. Advancing further in the interpretability, we have used Layer-wise Relevance Propagation, a Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanation technique to indicate CNN's decision-making rationale by selecting influential regions of input images. Our proposed GA-CNN model applied to a comprehensive oral image dataset resulted in a classification accuracy of 93.7%. Our sensitivity and specificity rates were 92.5% and 94.9% improvement over other CNN models available in the literature. We have demonstrated that our GA-based optimization mechanism performs better for parameter searching in the CNN. Our proposed AI tool with an explanation for oral cancer screening will assist clinicians in the early identification of disease, establishing a complementary relationship between human health service providers and machine learning technologies for improved patient outcomes.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Strategy for the Solution of Economic Load Dispatch Problem
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: The primary responsibility of load dispatch centers is to maximize economic efficiency while maximizing operational efficiency, which is achieved by minimizing the cost of real power generation at various generating units for any given load demand. This study introduces a hybrid approach combining Levy flights, Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), and Sine Cosine approach (SCA) to address the Economic Load Dispatch (ELD) problem. The LFPSO is utilized to locate the global optimum, while the SCA is employed to explore the local optimum. The suggested method is evaluated on the standard IEEE 30 bus system and the findings are compared with other techniques.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of TFET Structures for Low Power Sensor Design
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: The use of biosensors is growing in significance in the quickly evolving world of technology today. Due to their extensive utilization, biosensors have sparked a great deal of research, with scientists utilizing them to identify precise sites for biomolecules. There has been a lot of interest in FET-based biosensors because of its high noticing skill, low power, low cheap, label-free biomolecule detection, and CMOS cooperative on-chip combination. TFETs have the capability to create ultra-low quiescent current (~pA). Metrics like elevated Ion/I off ratio, reduced ambipolar leakage, repressed subthreshold slope value, and high I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ON</inf> current are needed to assess TFET characteristics. The manuscript also improves on current approaches and offers a summary of a number of sensitivity parameters. This paper will provide researchers with a quick overview of a future concept for TFET biosensors that will have easier manufacturing procedures and better performance.

articleTitle: IoT-Driven Digital Transformation in Low Voltage Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: As a DISCOM, maintaining low-voltage (LV) networks is a constant struggle. In Tata Power-Delhi Distribution (DDL), there are more than 24772 feeders, 16200 LV air circuit breakers, and 8000 feeder pillars. There was no automation in the LV network, and as a result, the breakdown teams received no first-hand information in cases of LV interruptions. To address the issue, the first large-scale Internet of Things (IoT) infrastructure in LV distribution network has implemented in Tata Power-DDL. The IoT server swiftly analyzes real-time outage data, LV network parameters and provides field crew firsthand information without any manual intervention. The IoT project reduces fault restoration time by 41%, leading to a 14.77% drop in customer complaints on LV ACB tripping and decreased technical losses. The success of this initiative highlights its efficacy in enhancing operational efficiency and customer satisfaction in the LV distribution network.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of BLDC Motor for Electric Two-Wheeler
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: This research paper employs MATLABI Simulink to construct and simulate an electric two-wheeler, incorporating a Brushless DC (BLDC) motor. The focus is on the analysis of key parameters, such as velocity, battery state of charge, and motor torque, to evaluate the performance of the electric vehicle (EV). The study presents a detailed examination of the velocity output, showcasing its correlation with desired speeds. Additionally, the analysis extends to crucial parameters like battery state of charge and torque, providing insights into the overall efficiency and energy consumption of the electric two-wheeler. This comprehensive assessment serves to enhance our understanding of the BLDC motor's impact on the vehicle's dynamics, emphasizing its significance in the development of efficient and sustainable electric mobility solutions.

articleTitle: Figures of Merit in High Frequency GaN-Based Parallel Split Gate Trench Power MOSFET Device
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: A parallel split-gate trench MOSFET (PSGT-MOSFET) with a vertical GaN device has been introduced for improving the trade-off between specific on-resistance (Ron) and figures of merit in high frequency (HF-FOM) using TCAD simulation. The PSGT-MOSFET yields superior performance by allowing higher drift doping by providing a thick field plate at the mid-trench region. As a result, the PSGT-MOSFET exhibits a 31 % smaller Ron, 10× reductions in HF-FOM (Crss x Ron), and 3x reductions in HF-FOM (QGD x Ron) with the same breakdown voltage in comparison to the TG-MOSFET. Consequently, the HF-FOMs have been improved, resulting in faster switching speeds, which makes them more efficient power conversion systems.

articleTitle: Model Predictive Control-Based Common Mode Voltage Reduction for Enhanced Performance of Induction Motor Drives
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: This paper addresses the reduction of common mode voltage (CMV) in induction motor drives, which can lead to issues such as common mode current, switchgear tripping, and premature bearing failure. The proposed approach minimizes CMV by reducing the number of transitions in the common-mode voltage. This is achieved through a particular configuration of inverter switches that leverages the device junction capacitance (DJC) effect present across switches in the OFF state. The study employs Model Predictive Control (MPC) for the induction motor drive, leading to a reduction in CMV and a decrease in torque and flux ripple. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed topology in mitigating CMV-related problems, thereby enhancing the overall performance and reliability of induction motor drives.

articleTitle: Decentralized Phasor Measurement Unit Data Management on the Ethereum Blockchain
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: PMU Contract is a Solidity-based smart contract implemented on the Ethereum blockchain that aims to simplify the decentralized management of Phasor Measurement Unit (PMU) data. Solidity., which is tailored for smart contract creation., is the core of this novel solution. PMUs are critical in monitoring electrical characteristics in power systems., and PMU Contract creates a safe and transparent environment for the smooth recording., registration., and retrieval of PMU data. This contract., with its strong foundation., helps to the integrity and accessibility of critical information in the ever-changing context of power system management. The proposed work concentrated on smart contracts used for power trading or microgrid applications since they affect not only financial losses but also the operational integrity of smart grids., making this research crucial. Also proposed smart contract provides the foundation for keeping and retrieving PMU data on the Ethereum blockchain., guaranteeing that only registered PMUs can record data. It also promotes openness by allowing anybody to query the recorded data for a particular PMU. The smart contract test scenario given here exhibits resilience in data recording., security measures., and historical data retrieval. The theoretical approach used in building and testing the contract is consistent with the Ethereum blockchain's core concepts of decentralized and transparent data management.

articleTitle: Modelling Simulation and Optimization of PI Controlled Wind Turbine Emulator Using Golden Eagle Optimization for Improved Performance of Stand-Alone Grid
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: This research paper aims to model and simulate the wind turbine emulator (WTE), which is required to build a test rig for wind turbine generator (WTG) condition monitoring. The WTE uses a D.C. machine to imitate wind turbine characteristics. Furthermore, the wind turbine's properties based on the findings of the simulation are spoken about. The research's observations and findings support the WTE's capacity to alter D.C. motor torque in order to simulate wind turbine rotor torque. This study shows how, when utilizing the golden eagle optimization technique for the wind turbine emulator model, optimal settings for the PI controller can be discovered that meet both the system's behavior and a performance index, such as absolute integral error (IAE). In orderto enhance the DC motor's performance, the PI controller is further tuned in this work utilizing the Golden Eagle optimization technique.

articleTitle: IBR Performance Issues: Potential Threat to Grid Stability and Security
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: The global commitment to achieving net-zero emissions has accelerated the integration of intermittent renewable energy sources (IBRs) into power grids. The power grids are expected to see IBRs forming the major portion of the generation mix. However, IBR performance issues have recently caused several grid events, leading to a serious threat to grid stability and security. This paper brings out the potential IBR performance issues experienced by grid operators around the world. The paper reviews some of the major grid events and discusses the reasons behind the failure of IBRs connected to the grid and increasing grid instability. The paper revolves around the failures and disturbances reported in the USA and India. The paper also presents recommendations that could be helpful for various stakeholders in meeting their renewable targets while ensuring grid stability and security.

articleTitle: Grey Wolf Algorithm for Area-Wise Allocation of EV Charging Stations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: The electrification of the transport sector plays an important role in ameliorating smart cities. With the tremendous increase in Electric Vehicles EVs, deployment of well-planned EV charging stations is mandatory. Also, the installation of a greater number of charging stations at a place creates congestion on the distribution network and on the traffic inflow of vehicles. One of the best strategies to reduce pollution in the transportation industry is to use an electric vehicle. The vehicle's battery needs to be charged, hence, charging stations are necessary. The additional power demand during the charging of electric vehicles is the root cause of the voltage drop and power loss in the distribution system. Placing the charging station at the ideal node is required to maintain a healthy voltage profile and the least amount of power loss possible. The allocation of electric vehicle charging stations over an IEEE 33-node radial distribution network is the primary focus of this paper. Three distinct zones have been created throughout the distribution network to offer charging stations at different points within each area. Every three separate locations now has a charging station. Using Grey Wolf Optimisation, the issue has been transformed into an optimisation challenge, and area-wise distribution is done for better EV penetration.

articleTitle: Improving Solar Water Pump Efficiency: Exploring Beta MPPT and V/f Control Strategies
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: This study investigates ways to enhance the efficiency of solar water pumps by examining the effectiveness of Beta Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) and V/f control strategies. The research explores how these methods can contribute to improved performance in solar water pumping systems. Through a comprehensive analysis, we aim to identify optimal settings and configurations for Beta MPPT and V/f control, ultimately enhancing the overall efficiency and reliability of solar-powered water pumps. The findings from this study provide valuable insights for designing more efficient and sustainable solar water pumping systems, contributing to advancements in renewable energy applications.

articleTitle: Convex Optimization Method for Modeling Energy Density of Supercapacitor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: Supercapacitors are gaining significance owing to their remarkable ability to develop advanced energy storage devices for future use. In this paper, we present a new approach used to optimize the energy density of supercapacitors using the convex optimization method in Python programming. The presented work explores the use of the convex optimization technique to study the energy density of a supercapacitor by optimizing its charging and discharging cycles. The proposed model shows that there is a progressive linear increase in the value of energy density with time.

articleTitle: Evaluating Switching Losses of High Voltage Rating Devices Using Cockcroft-Walton Circuit
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: The importance of DC-DC converters in providing dependable power conversion across changing voltage levels in modern energy systems cannot be overstated. The growing need for efficient power conversion solutions highlights the importance of optimizing switching device performance, which has a substantial influence on operational frequency and power loss inside electronic circuits. While the double pulse test is an important method for testing device operational characteristics, its traditional circuitry suffers from high power drive demands, cost inefficiencies, and safety problems. This paper investigates switching losses of high voltage rating devices i.e. wide band gap (WBG) devices, using a modified double pulse test by using the Cockcroft Walton circuit to create high DC voltage for double pulse testing using a small AC voltage source. Further, the switching losses have been analyzed for different SiC, and GaN devices using the proposed circuit.

articleTitle: Sliding Mode Control for DC Microgrid Powered by Solar PV, Fuel Cell and Energy Storage System with Pulsating Loads
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: This study proposes a sliding mode control (SMC) method designed for a DC Microgrid (MG) system that integrates a fuel cell with battery backup and a photovoltaic (PV) array with maximum power point tracking (MPPT) capability. Because of their potential for effective energy distribution and conversion in a range of applications, DC MGs are drawing a lot of interest. The integration of RES like PV arrays & fuel cells poses challenges in maintaining stable operation and optimizing energy utilization. The proposed SMC scheme is designed to regulate the DC bus voltage and ensure seamless transition between different operational modes, such as grid-connected and standalone operation. The MPPT algorithm implemented for the PV array maximizes the harvested solar energy under varying environmental conditions, while the fuel cell system with battery backup provides reliable power supply during periods of solar insufficiency or grid outages. Simulation output results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed SMC approach in achieving robust and reliable control of the DC MG system. The system exhibits fast dynamic response, accurate tracking of the maximum power point, and smooth transition between different operating modes. Comparative analysis with conventional control techniques highlights the superiority of the proposed SMC strategy in terms of performance and robustness. Overall, the proposed SMC-based control strategy offers a promising solution for increasing the efficiency, stability, and reliability of DC MG systems incorporating PV arrays with MPPT capability and fuel cell battery backup. This research contributes to advancing the development of sustainable and resilient power systems suitable for diverse applications, including remote communities, industrial facilities, and distributed energy network.

articleTitle: Design and Evaluation of a Power Efficient Phase-Frequency Detector with PVT Tolerance in 45 nm CMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: This study investigates the deployment of a phase frequency detector by utilizing 45 nm CMOS technology. The work involves designing and analyzing the proposed detector to evaluate its performance and capabilities within the specified technology node. The circuit achieves a operating frequency of 9.524 GHz, 326 n W of power usage and a phase noise of - 152.1 dBc/Hz. Notably, the proposed circuit is free from dead zone, and its layout is created in CADENCE Virtuoso XL. Additionally, the paper includes an analysis of Process, Voltage, and Temperature variations. Monte Carlo analysis is utilized to simulate the statistical variations in the process that influence the performance of the circuit. The findings contribute to advancing the understanding of phase frequency detection in advanced semiconductor processes, offering valuable insights into potential applications and improvements in integrated circuit design.

articleTitle: Integrating Solar Photovoltaic Systems with Multilevel Inverter Topology for Enhanced Grid Connectivity
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: The integration of customized power devices into so-lar Photovoltaic (SPV) systems holds significant promise, offering enhanced power stability, voltage and current ride-through capa-bilities, and controlled power flow. This study aims to evaluate the efficiency and effectiveness of a grid-connected system utilizing the Cascaded H-bridge (CHB) design with SPV as the primary DC source. A Simulink model for an SPV Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) controlled system employing a cascaded H-bridge Multilevel Inverter (CHB MLI) with bidirectional switches is developed. The study compares the performance of CHB MLIs at 7-level, 9-level, and L1-level, yielding precise simulation results.

articleTitle: Analysis and Optimization of Interleaved Ultra-Boost Converters for Solar PV Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach in high gain dc to dc ultra boost converter in open loop scheme. The proposed high gain dc-dc converter is based on quadric topology. Two coupled inductors are used which are connected as Parallel-Dual-Leg (PDL) and Interleaved Dual-Stage (ILDS). Through moderate duty cycle maximum output voltage, reduced voltage ripple in load side is achieved and switching losses are reduced compared to conventional boost converters along with faster transient response. A comparative analysis is also presented to validate the potential of the proposed converters. Finally, these Parallel-Dual-Leg Interleaved Dual-Stage (PDL-ILDS) converters are simulated in MATLAB/SIMULINK toolbox to demonstrate the suitability.

articleTitle: A Modified Disturbance Observer Based Speed Sensor-less Control of Syn-Rel Motor for Electric Vehicles with Solar PV and Grid Support
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: Speed sensor less control is an efficient technique for providing reliable, cost-effective, and stable drive system in electric vehicle (EV). Yet, obtaining accurate sensor-less control across the entire speed range poses a significant problem. This paper presents a modified disturbance observer (MDO) based speed sensor-less control of synchronous reluctance (Syn-Rel) motor. The presented technique utilizes the active flux (AF) concept of the Syn-Rel motor, which eliminates the variations in the estimated flux from the cross-coupling. The presented system's robustness is enhanced by its insensitivity to DC bias and high-frequency noise. The speed and position are estimated with enhanced quadrature PLL (e-QPLL) technique. In comparison to conventional and other speed estimation techniques, the presented technique is with minimal speed and position error. The presented system is integrated with solar PV array and grid for augmenting battery performance. The battery performance and range are improved utilizing roof mounted solar panel under running and at rest condition of the vehicle. Moreover, performance is also improved with battery charging using installed voltage source converter (VSC) acting as an on-board charger under standstill condition. The system is analysed and validated using MATLAB software. A comprehensive depiction of EV dynamics with improved motor battery performance is included.

articleTitle: Design and Development of a Web-APP Based User Interface to Control and Operate an Automated Mobile Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: Industry 4.0 includes IoT and smart production. With integrated smart digital technology, it enables the industries quick and efficient production and supply chain management. The autonomous mobile robot is one of the technologies that are widely used in various industries to increase the efficiency and safety of the workplace. The present paper relates to the design and development of a Web-App based User Interface (WUI) to operate and monitor the Automated Mobile Robot (AMR) or the Automated Guided Vehicle (AG V) in the industrial floor space. The AMR can be operated both manually and automatically using the designed WUI. The information of the AMR is shown in the WUI for monitoring. In this paper, it is also disclosed about the design and development of a novel electrical system for the AMR with different operational features. The electrical system has a protection feature to react during an emergency,

articleTitle: Design and Development of Power Quality Module for Smart Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: The integration of advanced Distributed Energy Resources (DER) is transforming the traditional power grid into smart grids. Real-time monitoring and management of power system parameters are essential due to the intermittent nature of renewable energy sources. The development of a Power Quality Monitoring Module for Smart Micro-grid, utilizing Smart Multifunction Meters (SMFM), Programmable Logic Controllers (PLC), and Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) systems, enhances efficiency, reliability, and sustainability. This study analyses power quality concerns such as voltage imbalances, fluctuations in frequency and voltage, as well as neutral currents providing energy management in real-time on a micro-grid. Voltage and frequency variations were assessed under different load conditions, while voltage imbalance and neutral current were estimated using mathematical formulas. The results comply with Indian Electric Standards, ensuring safe operation. PLC embedded measures facilitate automatic circuit breaker operation to maintain parameters within predefined limits.

articleTitle: Analytical Study of the Transient Period of Fault Current in Inverter-Based Resources
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: The increasing integration of inverter-based re-sources (IBRs) in modern power systems poses challenges to traditional grid conventions due to features such as low inertia and limited fault current supply. Since IBRs exhibit distinct fault characteristics compared to synchronous generators, a reevalu-ation of existing protection schemes is necessary. Understanding the transient response of IBR during faults is crucial for both protection system design and ensuring that its outputs remain within the maximum limits of internal semiconductor materials, which is a factor heavily influenced by manufacturer-specific con-trol settings. While electromagnetic transient programs (EMTP) provide valuable insights, their application to large power systems is computationally intensive, underscoring the need for analytical fault models. This paper addresses these challenges by converting EMTP models of grid-following IBRs into transfer function models to study transient response. Additionally, it attempts to derive fault current expressions for LC-filter-based inverters and identifies the corresponding factors that influence the resulting transients. The accuracy of the developed analytical model is also evaluated against simulations in PSCAD.

articleTitle: A 22kW OBC with Isolated DC/DC Converter with Bidirectional Power Flow for Electric Automobiles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: This paper presents a bidirectional on-board charging system with integrated DC/DC solution for electric automobiles. The charging system has three single phase AC-DC converters for active rectification and three DC-DC isolated converters for CC/CV charging of Li-ion battery. The AC-DC converter is controlled using SRF control approach and DC-DC converter is controlled using PWM control technique. A 22kW isolated charging system is designed with multi-objective features. A complete design procedure for each parameter is also shown. The charging control is validated through MATLAB/Simulink. A set of results are taken at various battery voltages for both charging and discharging operation. From different results, the effectiveness of PWM control for DAB DC-DC converter is verified. The effect of wide range of output voltage on amount of circulating current in primary and secondary side H-bridge is minimized using PWM control of DC-DC converter and it is justified using numerous results taken at different battery voltages during both charging and discharging operation. During discharging operation, the change in PWM switching frequency required to supply certain current at some minimum battery voltage is also justified.

articleTitle: Study on Impact of Inverter-Based Generation on Out of Step in Power System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: Recently inverter-based resources (IBR) significantly share power generation with conventional synchronous generators to meet the demand in the system. Apart of IBR's wide advantage, it has a critical disadvantage on the system stability by reducing overall system inertia. Among the stability issues presented by IBR, this paper focuses on angular stability, specifically the out of step (OOS) condition in power system. In this paper, an analysis has been carried out on the impact of low inertia effect on inter-area oscillation with extension to OOS condition in power systems. A new OOS prediction speed coefficient has been proposed in this study, which has been developed using Wide Area Measurement System (WAMS). The simulations in this study have been performed on benchmark systems using OPAL-RT real-time simulator in Hypersim environment.

articleTitle: Design of PV Automated Water-Cooling System with Varying Flow Rate
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: In the last ten years, solar energy systems have been utilized to generate electricity. However, efficiency improvement of solar panel overtime proves to be challenging for these studies such as the importance of Equal Distribution of water that results in uneven panel temperatures, Consideration of temperature for reuse water and an implementation of control system. Thus, this study aims to design an automated cooling system. The higher angles produce lower efficiency over time where the lowest angle 22 produces the highest output 12.48%. The Water Distribution test shows that setup 3 produces 11.24% efficiency which is more consistent compared to other setups. Efficiency over time shows that 3L/minutes perform the most consistent efficiency, having 11.96% compared to others. Solar panel temperature is indirectly proportional to L/mins. The statistical result summary table proves that most of the tests compared are significant and some tests are very significant.

articleTitle: Time Series Modeling Techniques for Solar Irradiance Forecasting: A Comparative Study
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: This study explores and compares advanced modeling techniques to accurately forecast short-term solar irradiance using data from a Solar Photovoltaic (PV) system in Phalodi, Rajasthan, India. The research utilized several time series models such as Linear Regression, ARIMA, LSTM networks, RNN, and Auto Regressors. After training the models with historical solar irradiance data from the site and validating their performance using a separate test dataset, it was found that LSTM and RNN models outperformed other techniques due to their ability to capture complex temporal dependencies in the data. This proficiency makes them ideal for short-term forecasting applications, which is crucial for efficient energy management and grid stability at the Solar PV site under investigation.

articleTitle: Design and Performance Evaluation of Various DC-DC Converters for Standalone PV Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: This paper presents the design, modelling, and simulation of a comparative study for boost, CUK, Single Ended Primary Inductor (SEPIC) and Quasi Z source converters for standalone photovoltaic (PV) systems. A Perturb and Observe (P&O) based controller for Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) is implemented to adjust the duty cycle of the DC-DC Boost Converter. This adjustment is made to align the source impedance with the load impedance, ensuring that maximum power is accurately tracked and delivered to the load, particularly amidst changing irradiation conditions. Design of these converters is carried to compute the optimum values of components such as inductor, capacitor and resistor to track maximum power. Performance of these converters is simulated in MATLAB2017a with 250 W VIKRAM Solar Panel and a resistive load. Various system parameters such as output voltage, current, power, ripple in current and voltage, efficiency and dynamic performance are compared under varying irradiance conditions. Detailed simulation results using Simp ower systems are presented for comparison and tabulated.

Author Keywords: Single Ended Primary Inductor and Quasi Z-source converter

articleTitle: Analysis and Design of LLC Resonance-Based ZCS Full-Bridge DC-DC Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: Proposed full-bridge DC-DC converter with a partial LLC resonance pulse is able to provide voltage clamping and zero-current switching (ZCS) for semiconductor devices. ZCS can be achieved by adding a small overlap between the switches on the same leg. It eliminates the voltage spike across the semiconductor devices by causing zero-current commutation. Additionally, pulse-resonance provides a lower circulating current, which lowers conduction losses and eliminates the need for overrated components. Variable frequency with fixed duty ratio modulation technique have been implemented in this converter. By using this modulation, converter operates with achieving ZCS for a wide range of source voltage variations. The resonant tank that is used in the converter eliminates the need for extra clamping circuitry that is typically needed in conventional current-fed converters. Consequently, the proposed converter has the advantages of a stiffer DC input current and a lower circulating current, which prevent overrated devices and increase efficiency.

articleTitle: Design of Buck Converters and Integration of Electrical with Software Subsystem for Interplanetary Rovers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: A rover is a small vehicle that can move over rough ground, often used on the surface of other planets, sometimes controlled from the earth. This paper presents the development and integration of a high-frequency buck converter system for interplanetary rovers, focusing on efficient power management. Leveraging the TI C2000 micro controller and MATLAB/Simulink, a setup of a 24V to 12V buck converter was created and simulated. The buck converter transfer function served as the basis for an auto-tuned Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) controller that provided accurate voltage regulation. The described buck can convert the prescribed voltage at high-frequency (200 kHz) without any delay that would hinder the rover outcomes. This research demonstrates the feasibility and effectiveness of this approach for powering critical rover electronics, contributing to reliable and efficient operation during future space missions.

articleTitle: Energy Optimization with Electrical Vehicles Optimal Pattern for Charging/Discharging in Smart Distribution Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: In this paper, we proposed a novel grid power minimization problem that considers the combined advantages of distributed generators (DG) and electric vehicles (EV) in a smart distribution system (SDS). At first, the distribution load flow (DLF) is simulated without considering the DG and EV, and then in the second stage, the DLF is evaluated considering the DG and EV. To evaluate the effectiveness, proposed method has been tested and validated on a standard IEEE 33-bus test system. The results obtained are analyzed and compared with the without DG and EV case and found that the grid power after the inclusion of DG and EV has been reduced by 70% of its earlier case. Further, the findings demonstrate a greater improvement in voltage profiles for all the buses in the analyzed radial test bus system. Furthermore, minimization of grid power along with DG costs, EV revenues and emissions are considered as multiple objectives in the future work.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Optimum Wall Slope of a Frustum Shape Solar Pond under Variable Ambient Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: A transient model is presented in connection with a frustum-shape solar pond for a one-year period. The pond area at top is taken to be sufficiently large such that wall shading effect is ignorable. Implicit finite difference method (FDM) has been used to solve the governing energy equation. Using this solution, temporal variation of lower-convective zone (LCZ) temperature is observed for different wall slopes, keeping the total pond volume and topmost area constant. It is seen that under mentioned constraints, LCZ temperature at every instant is larger for a larger wall slope. Thus, the best possible solar pond is attained at theoretically infinite wall slope, dignifying a cylindrical pond. Hence, the conclusion observed by the authors in previously published steady state model of the literature is reported to be true even for transient state, which is that a vertical walled solar pond is the best shape for maximum thermal output.

articleTitle: Decentralized Energy Consumption Monitoring RF Communication-Enabled Modules for Offline Buildings Connected to Cloud
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to energy consumption monitoring and management in remote, off-grid locations where internet connectivity may be limited. The proposed system employs wireless sensor modules strategically mounted on each building, equipped to read parameters related to energy consumption. These modules communicate data to a central controller using RF communication. The system integrates both grid power and solar solutions, providing a comprehensive overview of energy usage. The main controller, connected to the internet, uploads the collected data to the cloud, enabling centralized monitoring and analysis. This decentralized approach allows for real-time monitoring of energy usage in offline locations, facilitating more efficient energy management and resource allocation. The paper discusses the design, implementation, and preliminary results of the system, demonstrating its potential for enhancing energy sustainability in diverse environments.

articleTitle: Securing Microservice Architecture: Load Balancing and Role-Based Access Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: This study focuses on the security aspects within microservice architecture, particularly addressing load balancing and role-based access control (RBAC). Exploring the intersection of load balancing techniques and RBAC mechanisms, the research aims to enhance the security posture of microservices. By evaluating strategies for efficient load distribution and implementing RBAC protocols, the study seeks to fortify the architecture against potential vulnerabilities. The integration of load balancing and RBAC not only ensures optimized resource utilization but also strengthens access control measures, bolstering the overall security framework in microservice-based systems.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Solar PV-Array Powered CUK Converter Battery Charging
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: In this work, we use the MATLAB/Simulink modeling platform to show circuit modeling of an isolated system's lead-acid battery charging with MPPT-controlled solar photovoltaic. In the charge controller, DC-DC conversion is accomplished using a Cuk design. The Adjust and Track MPPT algorithm monitors the maximum force generated by PV systems. With lead acid batteries, the three phases of charging are known as peak power tracking, continuous voltage charging, and floating charge. The working hypotheses within the design are all tested in three key aspects against the MPPT charge controller simulation: MPPT tracking of performance, battery charging performance, and full efficiency of charge regulators. The results indicate the validity of MPPT can extract the PV system's highest point in less than 0.5 seconds, independent-end of the change in solar irradiation, and with an efficiency of 95.22-98.67%.

articleTitle: Investigation of Right Half Plane Zero in Voltage Regulated Non-Ideal Boost Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: The reduction in the effect of Right Half Plane Zero of a voltage regulated Boost converter considering lossy input inductor and lossy output capacitor is investigated in this paper. The control to output transfer function is derived for three cases for each non-ideality and a compensator is selected. The shift of RHP zero locations and stability margins are thoroughly investigated with the help of Bode plots and results are presented. Based on the investigation, conclusions are drawn to improve the closed loop performance of the Boost converter modifying the control loop design without any additional circuitry.

articleTitle: Pi Model-Based SoC Estimation of Li-Ion Battery for Different C-Rates
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel Pi model-based approach for estimating the State of Charge of Li-Ion batteries across a spectrum of charging and discharging rates, denoted as C-rates. The methodology encompasses the development and testing of the proposed Pi model, followed by a comprehensive evaluation under 1C, 2C, and 3C rates to assess its performance. Comparative analysis with a previously established model elucidates the superior accuracy and robustness of the Pi model, particularly noticeable under high C-rate conditions, such as 3C rates. Validation of the proposed model employs experimental battery data, ensuring its practical relevance and reliability. These findings underscore the potential of the Pi model to significantly enhance SoC estimation precision, thereby facilitating advancements in battery management systems crucial for various applications ranging from electric vehicles to renewable energy storage.

articleTitle: A Fuzzy and Taguchi Method Based Hybrid Approach for Coordinated Voltage Stability Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: The paper delves into the significance and challenges associated with On-load tap changers (OLTCs) in upholding power system stability and quality. Although OLTCs can adeptly regulate voltage levels under normal conditions, their operation may elevate the risk of voltage collapse when facing heavy loads. To tackle this issue, a two-stage coordinated strategy is proposed. Initially, heavily loaded critical transformers are identified, followed by the implementation of coordinated OLTCs and dynamic VAR compensators using the Taguchi method. A fuzzy multi-objective optimization problem is devised to fine-tune OLTC tap settings and dynamic VAR controller parameters, aiming for improved power system performance. The effectiveness of the approach is verified using the standard IEEE 30 test system.

articleTitle: A Gaussian Doped p-GaN HEMT for Power Electronics Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: This paper presents and investigates a novel p-GaN HEMT to enhance device performance in power electronics applications. The proposed device incorporates the Gaussian doping technique to introduce donor impurities into the GaN channel layer. The gradual and controlled incorporation of donor impurities using Gaussian doping facilitates a smooth doping profile, thereby reducing electric field variations at the channel interface. This precise control effectively mitigates gate leakage current, leading to an improvement in the off-state performance of the device. Moreover, comparative analysis reveals that the proposed device exhibits superior characteristics, including enhanced gate leakage current, maximum drain current, on-current, and transconductance, when compared to the conventional p-GaN HEMT with no doping in the GaN channel layer. Additionally, optimization procedures are implemented to achieve optimal device performance, particularly focusing on minimizing gate leakage current. Furthermore, comparison of performance parameters of the proposed device with the reported devices have been performed.

articleTitle: Design and Development of Synchronous Buck Converter for Battery Charging Application Supporting MPPT and CC-CV Mode
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: Solar energy has witnessed significant popularity with the rapid advancement of solar photovoltaic systems. Mod-ern commercial solar panels have achieved a conversion efficiency ranging from 17 % to 24 %, efficiently converting light energy into electricity. To further optimize solar energy utilization, various maximum power tracking algorithms have been proposed, with Perturb and Observe being the most commonly used due to it's robustness and ease of implementation. In the context of battery charging applications, the hardware design was tailored to support Constant Current-Constant Voltage (CC-CV) mode. The hardware-implemented synchronous buck converter to enhance its efficiency. This paper explores the integration of the Perturb and Observe algorithm in the hardware's design, focusing on its efficiency in maximizing solar energy extraction and its ability to support CC-CV mode for battery charging. The results highlight the successful implementation of the hardware design and the algorithm, emphasizing the hardware's effectiveness in optimizing solar power utilization and charging batteries efficiently.

articleTitle: Optimizing Building Integrated Photovoltaic: Energy Conservation Simulation by Using BEOPT Tool
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: Building Integrated Photovoltaics (BIPV) transforms sustainable energy generation by seamlessly incorporating solar technology into building structures. This detailed research gives an overview of BIPV, including its many forms, benefits, problems, and applications. The study, which emphasizes the fundamental link between architecture and renewable energy, focuses on the critical job of balancing BIPV system energy output with building energy use. To accomplish this, the research suggests employing existing renewable energy resources within the facility to guarantee that total annual energy consumption equals renewable energy output, resulting in a Net Zero-Energy building status. Using BEopt (Building Energy Optimization Tool) software makes this task easier, allowing students to examine residential building designs and propose cost-effective efficiency solutions. BEopt's versatility allows for the assessment of a wide range of building types, including single-family dwellings and multi-family structures, for both new construction and retrofit projects. BIPV emerges as a critical component in designing energy-efficient and aesthetically beautiful building solutions to meet the growing need for sustainable energy sources.
