Furthermore, in India, an energy conservation building code establishes minimum performance criteria for building envelopes, emphasizing the need of BIPV in achieving energy efficiency targets. This code is a helpful resource for engineers, architects, and stakeholders working on energy-efficient building designs in India.

articleTitle: SoC Based Adjustable Virtual Capacitor Droop Control for Supercapacitor in a DC Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: Battery-Supercapacitor based Hybrid Energy Stor-age System supports a DC Microgrid improving its power profile. The Supercapacitor reduces the stress on the battery storage system by supplying power in transient conditions. This enhances the battery performance with average power supply, through the varying load demands. In this work, the response of the SC with improvement in State of Charge (SoC) profile is carried out by employing the Virtual Capacitance Droop Control (VCD). It is proposed to continuously vary the droop coefficient in the VCD control, based on the DC link voltage and SC SoC. A DC Microgrid is simulated in MATLAB/SIMULINK platform to study the SC response when Pulsed Power Loads (PPL) are applied under heavy and light loaded conditions. Compared to the conventional fixed VCD control and switched-capacitor control, the proposed approach enhances the SoC profile of SC, and also the response of SC under transient conditions is improved.

articleTitle: Detection An H-Bridge -Based Topology for Cascaded Multilevel Inverters with Fewer Components
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: This article presents the case study of various cascaded multilevel inverter topologies. It includes a five-level cascaded H-bridge multilevel inverter and seven and thirty-one levels of cascaded H-bridge inverter topologies with two one-way power switches. Compared to traditional multilevel converters, the number of DC-voltage sources (DCVS), switches, blocking voltages, installation space, and converter costs needed to get the same results decreases drastically in the 7 and 31-level topologies. In this topology, the magnitudes of the necessary DCVS are calculated using special criteria. The construction of the suggested topology employs a minimal quantity of switches and DCVS while also generating a significant number of output voltage steps. The simulation results validate the suggested multilevel converter's functionality and efficacy, employing the closest voltage control technique. Furthermore, a comparative analysis is conducted with other commonly used topologies to assess their performance.

articleTitle: Investigation of Magnetic Characteristics and Force-Velocity Behavior of a Two-Wing Armature Electromagnetic Launcher
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: This study focuses on an Inductive-type Electromagnetic Launcher (IEL) consisting of a fixed core with coils and a movable armature designed to accommodate objects requiring linear motion. A 3D model of the IEL is developed using ANSYS. A 2D model using FEMM freeware is developed to observe flux lines, with ten flux tubes observed flowing through various components. The reluctance of the flux path is derived and presented, along with self and mutual inductances. A mathematical model of the IEL is developed using ANSYS Simplorer and a power circuit to analyze the output force and velocity. Simulations across a range of voltages show a force of 156 N and a velocity of 2 m/sec, demonstrating the model's feasibility for launching applications. The relationship between force and voltage is explored, indicating scalability for different forces, and the output muzzle velocity of 425 m/sec for 500V confirms its suitability for high-speed applications.

articleTitle: Sigmoid Least Absolute Difference based Control Algorithm for a Double-Stage Grid-Tied PV System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: Grid-tied photovoltaic (PV) systems have long had difficulties with power quality (PQ). In this work, a sigmoid cost framework-based Sigmoid Least Absolute Difference (SLAD) algorithm is presented for the control of Shunt Active Power Filter (SAPF) to be applied to enhance power quality in a double-stage grid-tied PV system by injecting harmonic components of load currents in shunt mode at the point of common coupling (PCC). A Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) application is used to extract the maximum possible power from the PV array. The performance of the proposed method is simulated in a MATLAB/SIMULINK setup under dynamic changes in load and atmospheric conditions and then compared with conventional control algorithms like synchronous reference frame theory (SRF or d-q theory) and discrete second-order generalized integrator (DSOGI) in terms of Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) of the grid current. The results confirm a reduction in Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) pursuant to IEEE-519 standard. Furthermore, through comparison, it is evident that the proposed control algorithm demonstrates better power quality performance, characterized by the least grid current THD.

articleTitle: An Input Context Layered Local Recurrent Neural Network for Nonlinear System Identification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: In this work, a new local recurrent neural network called as input context layered local recurrent neural network (ICLRNN) for identifying nonlinear system is introduced. ICLRNN is composed of one context layer at the input, one hidden layer and one output layer. This structure improves the network's ability to identify the variations in the system being studied. To demonstrate the effectiveness of the ICLRNN, it was applied to a nonlinear dynamical system and compared to a feed forward neural network (FFNN). The results show that the ICLRNN outperforms the FFNN, making it a promising choice for nonlinear system identification.

articleTitle: Lighting of Workspaces in Compliance with Standards
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: To ensure that employees are as efficient and generally satisfied as possible in performing their tasks, special attention needs to be given to adequate room lighting. The paper provides a detailed explanation of the lighting of workspaces, as well as the significance it has on the quality of human life. The requirements for efficient lighting are presented, and the standards used in this field are listed. Additionally, the method of lighting individual workspaces in the building of the Faculty of Electrical Engineering, University of East Sarajevo, is described. A practical example of lighting calculation in the Relux software package is presented. Concrete measures for improving the lighting of these workspaces are also proposed.

articleTitle: BiLSTM based approach for Energy Demand Forecasting and Synchronization among Smart Grids
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: Recent growth in industrialization and urbanization has increased pollution. Air pollution is one of the major concerns of this era. The main cause of air pollution is the use of fuel-based vehicles. Electric vehicles (EVs) are being used to reduce air pollution which has increased the demand for electric energy and created chaos. This study presents an innovative approach that enhances the synchronization among the various Stockholders in the smart grid (SG) system. The model is advantageous for several parties involved in the smart grid, such as power generation companies, owners of hybrid and electric vehicles (EVs), and electric vehicle charging stations. Charging stations serve as crucial intermediaries, ensuring a balance between demand and supply. A Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) network is at the center of this approach, with the objective to correctly predict the consumption of energy. In order to improve smart grid synchronization, our research utilizes data from PJM Interconnection LLC, a regional transmission organization. The paper compares the performance of various forecasting models on different evaluation metrics like MAE, MSE, RMSE, and MAPE. We got an MAE score of 26.15 and an RMSE score of 35.15, which are comparatively less than other models. The results show that the BiLSTM model is more effective at making predictions than other methods. This study not only contributes to the field of energy forecasting but also paves the way for more efficient and sustainable energy management in smart grid systems.

articleTitle: A Bridgeless High Step Down Voltage Gain Based Power Factor Correction Rectifier Fed Low Voltage Low Power Switched Reluctance Motor Drive
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: A bridgeless modified SEPIC based front end PFC rectifier is presented for low voltage low power switched reluctance motor (SRM) drive. Using switched inductor in traditional SEPIC converter, output voltage is reduced to meet low voltage DC link requirement of asymmetric bridge converter (ABC) fed SRM drive. Unlike, diode bridge rectifier-based SEPIC, presented bridgeless converter is more efficient as prime requirement of low power applications. Discontinuous conduction mode (DCM) operation is selected for low power to reduce controller complexity and cost of drive. Two switches are used in this bridgeless topology and their gate triggering pulse is independent of supply voltage information. Single voltage sensor is sufficient for wide voltage control for SRM drive. Inductors are selected to operate in discontinuous current conduction mode (DICM) for grid side power quality management per international IEC 61000-3-2 standard. DC link voltage regulation involves adjusting voltage level within system to ensure proper control and operation of motor. Bridgeless converter is designed for 400 W, 48 V, three phase SRM drive for domestic/industrial appliances. Component design and validation of presented power factor correction (PFC) rectifier fed SRM drive are presented through MATLAB Simulink. Simulation results affirm reliability of converter in maintaining unity PFC across a wide range of SR motor speed, even in presence of fluctuations in supply voltage.

articleTitle: Trading Strategies in Power Energy Sector
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: We are entering a period of facing double challenges - economic and energy. These challenges are deeply interconnected and often mutually reinforcing. Energy systems around the world face several problems: from increased demand for energy to deficiencies in infrastructure, as well as the impact of variations in the price of electricity. These problems require innovative approaches to electricity generation. This paper presents how electricity prices are formed and how trade is carried out at the level of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

articleTitle: A Simple Low Cost Electricity Generation Using Piezoelectric Crystals for Remote Areas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: This paper presents an easy, simple and low-cost electricity-generating scheme comprising piezoelectric crystals, which can be utilized in villages located in hilly and remote areas of developing countries, where electricity is still not accessible. The proposed system uses the vibrations produced by foot-steps of family members. The power generated is stored in a battery and can be utilized whenever needed. The prototype of the proposed system is prepared and the experiments were performed on it. The power stored in the battery is adequate in view of mobile charging and to supply power to light emitting diodes (LED), which can be used for providing light in working hours at night in villages of remote areas. The impact study to observe the variations in voltage and current generated by the varying stress produced by the different mechanical loads put on the piezoelectric crystals is also carried out in the paper.

articleTitle: Bayesian Regularisation Algorithm of Artificial Neural Network for Two Stage Grid Connected Solar Photovoltaic System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: This paper conveys a maximum power point tracking (MPPT) system based on an Artificial Neural Network (ANN); it is combined with the control module for a Two stage grid connected photovoltaic system (TSGC-PV) which also utilizes ANN. Before being implemented for the TSGC- PV system, the suggested backpropagation approach based on Bayesian Regularization is implemented to guide the ANN controller. By addressing the drawbacks of conventional control schemes, ANN based technique ensures minimized harmonic content, stable output signals, and beneficial power extraction under multiple atmospheric conditions and fluctuations. To assure the efficiency of the suggested controller, comparative simulation results are provided, taking into account various dynamic test scenarios like temperature and irradiance alterations during the day.

articleTitle: An Enhanced Gain Two Input Step-Up DC- DC Converter with Non Isolated Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: A hybrid power generation system balances the power supply by drawing from two or more sources. Therefore, obtaining benefits from other sources may be feasible. Additionally, the majority of non-conventional energy sources, such as solar arrays and fuel cells will have small output voltages. For practical application, this needs to be significantly increased, which can be done by utilizing multi-input converters. This study presents the introduction of a non-isolated two input high gain DC-DC converter. The converter makes use of a voltage multiplier cell to provide an enhanced voltage gain. Comprehensive examination of the converter has been carried out in multiple operational states under steady state conditions. The presented converter is thoroughly inspected, and the description of simulation and experimental data validates the converter's functionality.

articleTitle: Neurofuzzy Based MPPT for a Hybrid Powered BLDC Motor in Water Pumping Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: This paper presents the ANFIS based MPPT technique applied to a solar-PV and battery driven brushless DC motor for water pumping application. The sepic converter is considered in the solar photovoltaic arrays (SPVs) that allows soft starting of the motor. The battery is charged by SPV array when the water delivery is not required whereas the charged battery provides power under bad weather conditions and during the night. A bidirectional buck-boost DC-DC converter is utilised that allows the battery to automatically switch between the different modes of operation. The speed of the BLDC motor is controlled by a pulse width modulated control of the voltage source inverter utilizing a DC link voltage controller. The performance analysis of the proposed ANFIS controlled system is carried out in MATLAB/SIMULINK and the results are compared with the conventional P&O technique. It is observed that the voltage gets stabilized more quickly with a maximum power of 4.7kW as compared to the conventional technique.

Author Keywords: ANFIS(Adaptive network based fuzzy inference system)

articleTitle: Solution of Economic Load Dispatch for Dealing with Solar Power Uncertainty Using Pelican Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: The increasing need for sustainable and clean energy sources making system engineers difficult to provide stable supply of electrical power. Thermal power facilities follow the standards of Economic Load Dispatch (ELD) while accounting for fuel costs. On the other hand, non-conventional energy sources like wind and solar farms lower the costs for thermal power providers while simultaneously advancing sustainability goals. However, owing to its inherent unpredictability, the growing prevalence of these resources presents serious challenges to the power system's operation. Based on these aspects, this work utilizes a novel stochastic optimization algorithm named as Pelican Optimization Algorithm (POA) to address the ELD problem in the presence of source uncertainty. Here, the efficacy of POA is analyzed through various case studies. The convergence results for the universal IEEE bus system illustrate the algorithm's superior exploration capability and usefulness compared to its other counterparts.

articleTitle: An Experimental Investigation of Maximization of Output Power for the Different Position of Photovoltaic Panel with Minimal Area
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: This study focuses on the integrative experiment to explores the innovative strategies for maximizing the output power of photovoltaic panels through varied positions, coupled with a reduced panel area. By employing diverse orientations and controlled experiments, we aim to identify optimal configurations that balance energy efficiency with reduced spatial requirements. The research delves into the synergies between panel positioning and area reduction, offering insights into sustainable and creative approaches for enhancing the performance of photovoltaic systems in diverse environmental conditions.

articleTitle: Wireless Energy for Electric Vehicles using Solar Panel
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: This project outlines the development of a solar-powered wireless charging system tailored for electric vehicles, addressing the challenges posed by costly gasoline and harmful emissions. The solution offers an efficient, high-frequency charging approach that harnesses solar energy and wireless transmission for environmentally friendly and versatile EV charging. The system utilizes a solar panel with Incremental Conductance Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) to optimize power extraction, Boost converters to elevate output voltage, an inverter for DC to AC conversion, a high-frequency Ideal Transformer for power transfer, a rectifier to convert AC to DC supply, and a Buck Converter to amplify current suitable for battery charging and general use. The Buck converter integrates outer voltage PI control and inner current PI control to enhance output current. Through simulation with MATLAB/Simulink software, this technology demonstrates the feasibility of a road-integrated, solar-powered wireless charging solution for electric vehicles.

articleTitle: Analysis of Bifacial Photovoltaic Panel Under Different Reflective Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: With developments in bifacial solar panels, the solar photovoltaics interest has started shifting from monofacial designs to bifacial solar panels. This paper analyses and compares the performance between a bifacial and a monofacial solar panel system. The bifacial design offers different performance characteristics based on the reflective properties of the base material. This paper reviews and compares the system's performance on various reflective surfaces. This study employs a comparative outlook on performance measures such as current, voltage, power and thermal outputs. Taking the global energy crisis into consideration, solar panels prove to be an important replacement for the conventional ways of electricity generation and bifacial solar panels improve the efficiency of a conventional solar panel. Therefore, this study is anticipated to serve as a guide for integrating bifacial photovoltaic systems in general use, increase its efficiency and also promote research in this domain.

articleTitle: Adaptive Fuzzy Logic Based Controller for Grid-Interactive EV Systems in Charging Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: For efficient Grid to vehicle (G2V) operations, the harmonic power flow between Electric Vehicles (EV) and AC grid is required. This paper introduces an Adaptive control-based AC/DC converter that efficiently tracks the voltage and gives a robust control for dynamic loading conditions based on reference values in G2V Operation. The performance of the Adaptive Neural Fuzzy Controller is compared to that of a Neural Predictive Controller (NPC) and an Online-PI through a comparative analysis in G2V Operation. Three distinct controllers-Online-PI, Neural Predictive Controller, and Adaptive Neural Fuzzy Controller-are used to simulate a On-Board EV Charger using MATLAB/Simulink. In comparison to NPC and Online-PI controllers, the comparative analysis unequivocally shows that the adaptive neural fuzzy-based controller is more effective.

articleTitle: The Performance Analysis of 5-Level DC-AC Converter with Level Shifted PWM Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel reduced-count 5-level DC-AC converter topology designed for applications of medium voltage and high-power. The proposed topology comprises a single cell of Conventional CHB MLI, utilized for polarity generation, and a diode switch combination for level generation. it is extendable topology like a CHB MLI with reduced count of switches. A new metric called the index switch requirement ratio (SRR) is introduced to determine the cost-reduction of the proposed topology compared to existing CHB MLI topologies for L levels. Level shift pulse width modulation techniques are employed for generating firing pulses in the proposed topology. The performance assessment of the proposed topology is conducted through the analysis of total harmonic distortion (THD) using level shift PWM techniques, including Phase Disposition (PD), Phase Opposition Disposition (POD), and Alternate Phase Opposition Disposition (APOD) PWM, with different amplitude modulation indexes. The finding highlighted that proposed topology outperforms in PD PWM techniques.

articleTitle: Analysis and Design of Artificial Neural Network Based Droop Control for Autonomous Hybrid Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: Microgrids have become a valuable approach for incorporating distributed generation into broader power systems, though they face challenges in maintaining consistent voltage and frequency during autonomous load sharing. In addition, the injection of perturbations of loads has the potential of reducing the power quality of the system. Traditional droop control is used for effective load sharing, frequency and voltage stabilization among multiple parallel inverters but is sensitive to load change and accurate coefficient parameters. To overcome these challenges artificial neural network (ANN) based droop control is proposed. Proposed microgrid integrates a PV system and wind energy conversion systems (WECS) as multiple distributed generations (DG) through parallel connected inverters. The modeling of a microgrid operating in island mode was carried out using MATLAB/SIMULINK. Results demonstrate the accuracy of the Artificial Neural Network (ANN) based control strategy in managing load fluctuations and minimizing the total harmonic distortion of the inverter output.

articleTitle: Influence of Stator and Rotor Slots Combination on Induction Motor Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: Electric motors have a wide range of applications in the industry, and there are various types of these motors that offer different design features and functionalities. Among this diversity, induction motors stand out as a prominent motor type due to their widespread use and durability. Although induction motors are widely used, stator and rotor slots combination selection is still a challenge. In this study, the performance of two different three-phase squirrel cage induction motor models with 15 kW, 4 poles, 36 stator slots and 28 and 44 rotor slots, respectively, is examined. Models are analyzed with a computer-based analysis software. As a result of the analysis, the output performances of induction motor models are examined. Analysis results show that incorrect slot combinations selection reduces motor efficiency and causes synchronous torque. As a result of the study, the effects of correct and incorrect stator-rotor slots combination selection on induction motor performance are discussed.

articleTitle: Induction Machine Drive With The Space Vector Modulation (SVM)
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: In this paper, space vector modulation (SVM) is attractive for the field oriented control of Induction Machine (IM) drive. Fundamental theory is highly discussed with good postulation and detailed investigation as extension of robust modeling and simulation of the three phase Induction Machine (IM) driving system fed by three- phase inverter power supply

articleTitle: Application of Artificial Neural Network in Renewable Energy-Based Building Cooling Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: This paper introduces an artificial neural network (ANN) assisted machine learning model for a vapour absorption radiant air-conditioning system (V ARACS). The V ARACS was primarily operated with solar and natural gas/biogas energies. ANN outputs include, necessary cooling capacities of the chillers as well as necessary thermal loads imposed on the gas boiler, solar collector and the electric heater. Input data sets under variable ambient conditions were taken from EnergyPlus simulations. Three parameters: radiative intensity, ambient air temperature, and environment's relative humidity, were considered as inputs to the ANN. A total of 2591 input and output datasets were used, of which 80 % data were consumed for training, whereas 10% each were involved for validating and testing. The proposed ANN offered prediction of the cooling capacity with correlation coefficient of above 90 %. However, due to more irregular pattern of the heating load, its prediction accuracy was lower for this case.

articleTitle: Embedded Investigation of Synchronous Reluctance Motor Drive for Electric Two Wheeler
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: Achieving carbon net zero, a crucial goal for the electric vehicle (EV) industry, is hampered by the reliance on limited permanent magnet resources imported from abroad, which form the core of motor drives. To address this challenge, this paper explores the synchronous reluctance motor (SynRM) as a viable alternative. SynRM technology readily leverages existing manufacturing capabilities, offering a cost-effective solution. We investigate the performance of a 2.2 kW SynRM drive specifically designed for the EV two-wheeler industry. Based on extracted motor parameters, a mathematical model is developed to facilitate a thorough steady-state analysis of its performance characteristics. The model's accuracy is further validated through simulations conducted using MATLAB/Simulink software. Finally, a hardware prototype is designed and implemented using a Texas Instruments DSP TMS320F28335 to verify the theoretical and simulated findings.

articleTitle: Hilbert Curve Repositioning Algorithm for Reconfiguration of Partially Shaded PV Array
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: Partial shading (PS) poses a significant challenge for photovoltaic (PV) systems, leading to reduced energy output and multiple peaks in the Power-Voltage (P-V) curve. Shaded cells produce less power, impacting overall array output and potentially causing hotspots. This paper introduces the Hilbert Curve Repositioning Algorithm (HCRA), a static PV reconfiguration method designed to robustly address the adverse effects of PS on PV arrays. HCRA emphasizes optimal shade dispersion under PS conditions and enhances energy utilization through strategic module placements. Simulations in MATLAB Simulink, covering various shading patterns, evaluate metrics such as global maximum power point, mismatch loss, fill factor, and power loss to validate efficacy. Results illustrate increased power output, reduced power loss, and minimized mismatch loss, outperforming existing PV reconfiguration techniques. HCRA effectively mitigates the negative impacts of PS while demonstrating scalability and efficacy, emerging as a promising algorithm for enhancing output and reducing costs in PV plants.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of PEM Fuel Cell Using Various Smith Predictor Configurations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: With the advancements in green energy research, Proton Exchange Membrane (PEM) fuel cells have gained prominence in the field of energy storage and are becoming an alternative to IC engines in automotives. Fuel cell performance is dependent on factors like air and hydrogen feed, heat and water flow management etc. In the present work, various Smith predictor (SP) control design strategies are implemented on a PEM fuel cell process model and effective control techniques are determined. Robustness analysis is carried out by introducing uncertainties in the process model. Simulation results are attained using MATLAB software and performance is compared using time domain analysis, error analysis and control effort.

articleTitle: loT-Enabled Power Factor Monitoring and Correction with PZEM Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: The Automatic Power Factor Monitoring and Correction (APFMC) to enhance power factor close to unity. Power factor, a metric indicating the effectiveness of electrical power utilization, is crucial for reducing energy wastage and enhancing system efficiency when maintained close to unity. At the core of the APFC system is the ESP32 microcontroller, which acts as the central processing unit. The ESP8266 is a versatile microcontroller known for its processing power and built-in connectivity options, making it well-suited for applications requiring real-time data processing and communication. The APFC system establishes communication with the PZEM -004 T power monitor module. This module is responsible for gathering real-time data on essential parameters such as voltage, current, power, and frequency and Energy. This data provides the necessary information for the APFC system to analyze the current power factor and determine the required corrective actions. The APFC system includes four sets of capacitor banks, each with capacitors of varying capacitances. Capacitors are used in power factor correction to offset the effects of inductive loads, which can lead to a lagging power factor. By strategically adjusting the capacitance levels of these banks, the APFC system can achieve an optimal power factor across different operational scenarios. The ESP8266 continuously monitors the power factor and dynamically responds to deviations from the desired value. It achieves this by controlling relay switches that connect or disconnect specific capacitors in real-time. This intelligent switching mechanism allows the APFC system to fine-tune the overall capacitance, ensuring maximum efficiency in power factor correction.

articleTitle: SOC-Llama: Estimation of SOC Using Llama Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: Electric Vehicles are replacing the conventional combustion engines vehicles due to a number of advantages like less emissions, use of cleaner fuel etc at a high pace. They work on batteries which are basically operated on the principle of charging or discharging of cells. Therefore, SOC or state of the charge plays a vital role in monitoring and managing the informed decisions pertaining to recharging, optimizing battery life, and ensuring a smooth driving experience. SOC in other words helps in reflecting battery performance. SOC (State of Charge) is different from SOH (State of Health) as SOH assesses long-term battery health, while SOC indicates current charge levels. In this research paper, we aim to study the impact of various parameters like throttle, longitudinal acceleration, elevation, motor torque, regenerative braking, battery current, battery voltage, ambient temperature on SOC and develop a deep learning model using the LLama architecture.

articleTitle: Design Analysis of Outer Rotor PMSM for EV Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: The intend of this paper is to design a highly efficient outer rotor permanent magnet synchronous motor. Among inner and outer rotor configuration, the outer-rotor permanent magnet synchronous motor (OPMSM) has the convenience of immense torque density. Since, permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) has the advantage of prominent efficiency, high power and torque density and its compact size, it can be chosen for electric vehicle (EV) application. In order to accurately estimate the EMF and other parameters of PMSM, the design has been carried out in RMxpert employing ANSYS software. A 1.5 kW, 1500rpm OPMSM has been designed and the performance of torque, speed, airgap and efficiency has been analyzed. This toolkit provides a better outcome in anticipating the EMF and flux distribution of PMSM through Maxwell 2D/3D design.

articleTitle: Unobtrusive Optimization: Passive Cell Balancing for Enhanced Battery Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: Passive cell balancing is a widely employed technique in battery management systems (BMS) aimed at equalizing the state of charge (SoC) or voltage among individual cells within a battery pack. Passive balancing relies on dissipating excess energy from cells with higher voltage as heat or redirecting it to cells with lower voltage through passive components like resistors. This paper provides an overview of passive cell balancing methodologies, including circuit configurations and operation principles. Various factors affect the effectiveness of passive balancing, such as cell characteristics, pack configuration, and balancing circuit design. The paper accomplishes with a discussion on the practical applications of passive cell balancing in battery management systems, emphasizing its role in enhancing battery performance, extending lifespan, and ensuring safety in diverse applications ranging from portable electronics to electric vehicles and grid energy storage systems. Passive balancing of the battery is simulated in Matlab.

articleTitle: Balanced Power Distribution Control Strategy of A DC-DC Converter and Energy Storage System by Using Soc Management
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: The study's goal is to create a DC-DC modular multilevel converter-based supercapacitor energy storage system (MMC-SESS) that can help with peak load shifting in DC power grid energy storage applications on ships. It is the goal of this study to look into the control problems that come with the converter and to improve the current loop of the MMC-SESS by adding control for the supercapacitors' state of charge (SOC). The fuzzy immunity algorithm is being used in place of the traditional PI controller in order to improve the dynamic performance of the loop that is currently being used. As a means of establishing equilibrium, the SOC balancing loop makes use of the maximum SC voltage as its potential objective. As a consequence of this, modules that have a low SOC are able to control the average current of the sub-modules by using a reference value and their own SOC as the basis for the regulation. Therefore, the current flowing through the system will deviate from the recommended value as a result of the negative duty cycle that the SOC balancing loop of each sub module produces. A current compensation loop should be established as soon as possible in order to reduce the amount of variation in the system's current. For the purpose of determining whether or not the suggested method is effective, a simulation model is ultimately developed with the help of MATLAB and Simulink. Taking into consideration the findings, it seems that the existing degree of control accuracy and reaction speed has been enhanced. The possibility exists that the suggested approach might successfully offer SOC balancing control throughout the whole of the charging and discharging operations, hence providing an additional benefit.

articleTitle: Stability Enhancement for PV and Wind Penetrated Power System Using Machine Learning Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: In modern power systems, the integration of distributed generation (DG) has introduced both opportunities and challenges. It has also gained significant attention due to its potential benefits in terms of renewable energy utilization, improved system reliability and reduced transmission losses. As PV and wind are intermittent variables of the power system, stability problems arise which can be recovered using conventional PID controllers through the advanced tuning methods which incorporate the AI based tuning parameter. The process of tuning of the parameter is approached through proper artificial intelligence based trained data. This approach will enhance the power angle stability of the existing system.

articleTitle: Improved Mountain Gazelle Optimization for PID Tuning of MPPT Based Solar PV System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: Recent advancements in the field of solar energy has made a huge revolution in power generation. Due to the erratic nature of the system, there is a need to extract the maximum available power from the solar photovoltaic system at a given time. To extract the maximum power, we use power electronic converters. This paper uses a dc-dc boost converter for maximum power point tracking (MPPT) of the solar photovoltaic (PV) system using a proportional-integral-derivative (PID) controller. The PID controller is tuned using the improved Mountain Gazelle Optimization (MGO) algorithm. The performance of the controller is compared with other controllers tuned by optimization methods such as Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Grey Wolf Optimization (GWO) algorithm. The simulation studies were carried out using MATLAB and the results are presented.

articleTitle: Virtual Impedance Control for Enhanced Current Limitation in Grid-Forming Inverters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: Grid-forming inverters (GFM) are a promising solution for increasing renewable energy penetration in power system networks. Adapting to dynamic changes in grid conditions, ensuring coordination with other inverters, and tuning and calibrating current-limiting parameters are crucial issues in GFM-based systems. GFM-based systems must ensure fault current contribution, current magnitude limitation, and fault recovery capability to support the grid and protect power semiconductor devices under strict disturbances. Various methods are described in the literature to limit the current, i.e., virtual impedance, current limiters, and voltage limiters. This paper suggests a virtual impedance-based approach that adjusts the internal induced voltage to maintain system synchronization and track system voltage changes. The technique inhibits phase angle change by regulating the current and avoids grid instabilities. The paper addresses challenges like temporary transient overcurrent and current saturation. Simulations are conducted to demonstrate performance. Results ensure the control scheme's robustness and reliability.

articleTitle: Analysis of Trench Gate IGBT with GaN-AlN Dielectric Stacking
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: This article involved doing an analysis on the Insulated Gate Bipolar Transistor (IGBT) Using Wideband gap Materials. The investigation focused on increase the Performance of the device by changing the oxide material. The utilization of a stacked GaN/AIN (10nm,173nm) combination as gate dielectrics was found to yield improved outcomes in terms of Breakdown Voltage and Threshold Voltage. The proposed gate engineering technique demonstrates a significant enhancement in the Breakdown Voltage, with an approximate increase of 21 % when compared to traditional devices.

articleTitle: Optimizing Quadcopter Trajectory Tracking with Deep-Q Reinforcement PID Controller in Uncertain Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: Autonomous PID tuning is a compelling yet challenging application given the complicated dynamics of quadcopters, especially in unsafe environments. This study presents innovative PID variants, including Deep Q-Reinforcement Learning (RL-Q) PID, which aim to improve the stabilization of quadcopters. Using MATLAB, a comparative analysis with a conventional PID controller to determine their respective performance. To thoroughly evaluate their effectiveness, simulations are performed for two different trajectories-a circular and a dynamic spiral path. The simulation outcomes consistently reveal the superior performance of RL-Q PID compared to the standard PID. The RL-Q PID consistently outperforms, showcasing its advanced capability to stabilize the quadcopter on challenging traj ectories. These results provide valuable insights for the further development of control algorithms for quadcopter trajectory tracking and highlighting the performance of the proposed RL-Q PID, particularly in navigating uncertain and dynamic environments.

articleTitle: Effect of Strain on K2ScAgCl6 Halide Double Perovskite for Solar and Thermoelectric Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: This paper investigates halide double perovskite K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>ScAgCl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf> for the effect of strain on the structure by using full-potential augmented plane wave plus local orbitals FP-APW+lo method based on Density Functional Theory. Structural parameters are investigated using generalized gradient approximation with Perdew-Berke-Ernzerhof for solids (GGA-PBEsol) approximation which shows indirect bandgap of the pristine structure. Compressive strain reduces the bandgap of the structure whereas tensile strain produces a direct band structure. Optical and thermoelectric parameters are computed to observe the effect of strain on K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>ScAgCl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf> for solar and thermoelectric applications. Absorption, Optical conductivity and Electronic Figure of merit increases, and Energy loss decreases by applying Compressive stain on the material.

articleTitle: Miniature BLDC Motor in Nano Reaction Wheel for Small Satellites and Space Robots/Free-Flyers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: Nanosatellites become popular due to the fast-growing satellite industry and the demand for clustered space elements. The scope and applications of nanosatellites have increased with the advancements in Space Robots. The optimum sizing and minimal footprints are its major highlights. A three-phase, 12-pole BLDC motor is being used for the high-speed rotation of the flywheel. The drive motor configuration is thoroughly studied, and an enclosed type double rotor configuration has been selected to reduce the magnetic losses and, hence, the steady state power demand of the wheel. FE simulation analysis is carried out in detail to optimize the magnetic circuit of the motor so that the torque to rotor volume and power density of the motor is increased. The realized motor is tested for the Back EMF and developed torque, and the required torque constant is established. Design improvements and modifications to the existing BLDC motor are projected to cater to the requirements of Space Robot. Hermetic sealing of the wheel is required to avoid the loss of lubrication due to moisture contamination. Instead of the traditional way, the adhesive bonding-based process is implemented for the hermetic sealing of casing assembly. The major challenges in achieving an optimized BLDC to satisfy the mission/project requirements are also addressed.

articleTitle: Bypass Switch Type Single Phase Differential Cuk Inverter With Improved Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: The dual-stage conversion (DC to AC voltage conversion with a high voltage gain) process can be streamlined into a single-stage by adopting an innovative inverter topology known as the differential mode inverter (DMI). Compared to the two-stage conversion, the single-stage DMI enhances the compactness and energy density of the system while maintaining the same power rating. Within the DMI framework, a heightened voltage gain can be achieved by employing a designated DC-DC converter module. A differential mode inverter is developed in this paper using two Cuk converters with bypass switches. The Cuk converter stands out as a highly versatile DC-DC converter, offering advantages such as minimal output ripple voltage and continuous input and output current, which is best suitable for solar PV applications with an MPPT controller. Researchers still face challenges in differential mode inverters, particularly in achieving low peak-to-peak source current, efficiency and implementing effective control schemes. This topology offers high efficiency and low peak-to-peak source current as compared to other differential mode inverters.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of DC-DC Buck Converter with Type III Compensator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: This paper outlines the design methodology and circuit simulation of a buck converter. A compensator is incorporated to enable closed-loop feedback, ensuring stable operation. The paper also demonstrates the time-domain variation of the simulation under varying loads and reference voltages. Through meticulous design and simulation, the buck converter's performance is evaluated, with particular focus on its ability to regulate output voltage and respond dynamically to changing operating conditions. This comprehensive analysis sheds light on the converter's behavior and highlights its suitability for practical applications in power electronics.

articleTitle: Digital Twin Based Health Monitoring of DC-DC Converter: A Review
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: This review article provides a qualitative description of health monitoring for the DC-DC converter using the digital twin concept. A Digital Twin is a virtual clone of a physical system that operates simultaneously with a physical DC-DC converter. It provides data for monitoring and controlling the converter by using measurement data from existing sensors in the hardware. A digital twin might be either model-based, data-driven, or a hybrid of both approaches. This work presents the creation, advancement, and experimental confirmation of a digital twin method for monitoring the health of the DC-DC converter. Parameter deterioration and Fault Diagnosis are the primary factors that determine the health of the DC-DC converter. Determining degradation characteristics and identifying faults in the physical system relies on analyzing data by comparing sensor measurements with data from the digital model. This presentation discusses and compares several methods for assessing the status of the DC-DC converter.

articleTitle: Fault Analysis in Power Transmission Systems Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: With the increasing complexity and decentralization of power generation and consumption, the demand for robust fault detection and classification systems in power distri-bution networks has become paramount. This project addresses this challenge by employing machine learning techniques for the detection and classification of faults in the power distribution network. For fault detection, three models, namely Decision Tree, Sup-port Vector Machine (SVM), and Random Forest, are utilized to analyze electronic metrics and data. These models prove effective in identifying and localizing faults within the network, providing a foundation for proactive maintenance. In the classification phase, Decision Tree and SVM models are employed to further categorize detected faults. The integration of these models enhances the system's ability to not only detect faults but also classify them. The results indicate that the Random Forest model demonstrates exceptionally high accuracy in fault detection, outperforming other models. In the classification phase, the Decision Tree model exhibits superior performance, providing precise categorization of detected faults. This research delves into innovative methods for predicting network faults, with a particular focus on overhead lines. The proposed approach, backed by the success of the Random Forest and Decision Tree models, demonstrates high accuracy rates using various classifiers, contributing to the development of a comprehensive fault management system.

articleTitle: Comparison of PID Tuning Methods For Buck Converter System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: The most widely used Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) controller's effectiveness relies heavily on optimal gain tuning. While manual tuning methods prove to be cumbersome and may yield suboptimal results; this research paper investigates three advanced techniques for automated PID tuning: Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR), Genetic Algorithm (GA), and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). Each offers distinct advantages and limitations. This paper conducts a comprehensive comparative analysis of these three PID tuning techniques. We employ them to tune controllers for a buck converter system and assess their performance based on key metrics like rise time, settling time, and overshoot.

articleTitle: Recurrent Addition Based Static Reconfiguration Approach for Improved PV Power Extraction Under Partial Shading Condition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: One of the main environmental factors affecting photovoltaic (PV) systems' maximum power (MP) output, complexity of Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) because of the production of multiple peaks, and durability is partial shading (PS). To protect PV systems from the above negative effects of PS, innovative reconfiguration method based on the recursive addition methodology is described in the current article. This innovative method attempts to maintain a consistent row current by moving the panels physically even though maintaining the electrical connections the same. A <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$9\mathrm{x}9$</tex> Photovoltaic array with short-narrow, short-wide, long-wide, and random shading patterns is used in this study to test the efficacy of the proposed methodology using software models. The proposed method's functionality is also contrasted with other static reconfiguration strategies that have been put forth in the past, and it is found to perform better under every shade pattern that the current work takes into consideration.

articleTitle: Implementing ML and DL Based Controllers for Improving Efficiency in EV Charging Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: This paper analyzes the potential of various Machine Learning and Deep Learning algorithms for replacement of the traditional Proportional Integral (PI) Controller in a single-phase two-stage on-board Electric Vehicle (EV) charging system to improve its adaptability and efficiency. Traditional PI controllers, though reliable, often do not perform optimally under the dynamic demands of EV charging, leading to in-efficiencies. Our investigation aims to understand how these ML/DL methodologies can better handle the variable nature of EV charging through adaptability, accuracy, and efficiency in managing charging operations. Experimental results from both simulations and real-world data reveal the effectiveness of these ML/DL models in enhancing charging system performance over standard PI controllers. Decision Trees provide clear, rule- based control paths; Neural networks excel in modeling complex, non-linear relationships for real-time predictions; and Linear Regression offers a straightforward approach for linear charging dynamics.

articleTitle: Towards Sustainable Solar Energy: AI Based Multiple Anomaly Classification in PV Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: This paper investigates the use of Artificial intelligence (AI) techniques in the Solar Photovoltaic systems for measuring the health of the PV systems. It focusses on comparisons of different results generated by different deep learning networks models which are available in MATLAB like SqueezeNet; GoogLeNet. A total of eleven anomalies in PV module had been incorporated. The study also evaluates the accuracy and efficiency of these models in detecting faults and anomalies in solar PV modules. By analyzing the performance of CNN AI models, this research aims to provide insights into the effective approach for monitoring the health of PV systems.

articleTitle: Solar PV Powered Electric Vehicle Charger Based on ISSB Converter with Ripple Cancellation Circuit
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: This work deals with the design and analysis of ISSB (interleaved soft-switched boost) converter combined with a ripple cancellation circuit for a solar PV (photovoltaic) powered on-board EV (electric vehicle) battery charging system. The proposed ISSB converter configuration ensures efficient flow of solar PV output current and power hence optimizing the performance of the solar PV panel for electric vehicle charging system. The integration of a ripple elimination circuit with the ISSB converter not only reduces ripples in solar PV output current nonetheless notably, this circuit operates independently for duty cycle control. The incorporation of the ripple elimination circuit eliminates the necessity for an electrolytic capacitor along with the solar PV array. Detailed findings of the analysis and results obtained through simulations is presented to encapsulate the working of the developed system.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation Analysis of an On-Board Charger Using Different Control Strategies
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: The world is witnessing a significant shift toward electrification, with On-Board Chargers (OBCs) playing a crucial role in the electric vehicle (EV) revolution. OBCs act as power adapters within EVs, converting AC power from the grid into DC for charging while ensuring faster charging on the go. Effective OBC performance relies on power electronic converters and suitable control strategies that govern them. This study focuses on the Zeta converter topology controlled by Proportional Integral (PI) Control and Fuzzy Logic Control (FLC). Additionally, Power Factor Correction (PFC) is addressed to optimize active power transfer from the grid to the EV. The design and analysis of the OBC is done in MATLAB-Simulink which contributes to determine the efficiency of the On-Board Charger as evaluated through simulation results.

articleTitle: Enhancing Short-Term Load Forecasting for Distribution System Planning Using M-RMR and RNN Based Regression Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: Short-term load forecasting (STLF) plays a pivotal role in the efficient planning of distribution systems. It is a critical aspect that directly impacts the optimization of distribution system planning and operation, especially in the face of increasing demand and grid complexity. This study presents an improved approach to enhance the accuracy of STLF using a combination of Minimum Redundancy Maximum Relevance (m-RMR) and various Recurrent N eural Networks (RNNs). The RNN models include Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), and Bidirectional Long Short- Term Memory (Bi-LSTM). The integration of these two enables the model to effectively learn from high-resolution historical load data and deliver accurate forecasts. Importantly, the reduction in features also speed up the training process, making the models more time-effective. The simulations are performed on real-world electricity load datasets. To demonstrate its superiority over other standalone models, the comparison is performed using various validation metrics such as mean square error, mean absolute percentage error, mean absolute error, r squared error and root mean square error.

articleTitle: Investigation on Impact of Inverter Based Renewable Energy Sources on Distance Relaying
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: Prevention of blackouts in power system can be carried out to a large extent with protection schemes of transmission lines. Distance relaying are widely used for protection of the transmission line. However, due to rapidly increasing renewable energy sources in the power system whose behavior is different compared to conventional synchronous generators during fault condition shall lead to malfunctioning of these relays. This research study investigates the effect of renewable energy sources(RES) into the distance relaying. For this purpose IEEE benchmark nine bus system with PV farms has been considered to analyze the behavior of distance relays. It can be inferred from this study the incorporation of RES in the power system may lead to maloperation of relay or delaying in tripping time which may cause instability in the power system. Simulation study has been carried out in HYPERSIM OPAL RT real time simulator.

articleTitle: Multi-Functional Capabilities of Self Tuned Filter in Three Phase Four Wire Polluted Grid Distribution System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: Multifunctional capabilities of Self Tuning Filter (STF) for various applications in power distribution system are studied in this paper. These applications include the design of a new Phase Locked Loop (PLL), load compensation and extraction of fundamental and other higher order harmonic components from the distorted signals. It is well known that conventional PLL viz. Synchronous Reference Frame (SRF) PLL does not perform well for polluted grid voltages. Hence, there is a need to design new PLLs for grid synchronization. The performance of the proposed STF-PLL for normal as well as polluted grid conditions in Three-Phase-Four-Wire systems (TPFW) is investigated in this paper. Additionally, detailed analysis of STF-PLL is discussed for other applications viz. active filtering and harmonic estimation. Multiple applications of STF in a TPFW distribution system are presented for improving Power Quality (PQ). Experimental results on a prototype system using dSPACE 1104 are discussed to highlight usefulness of STF in wide ranging applications.

articleTitle: Identification of Lines Connecting Coherent Areas in Power System for Safe Islanding
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: Coherent areas can be formed in power systems that oscillate against each other after a contingency. Identification of lines that connect these coherent areas for safe islanding is essential prior to reaching out-of-step condition between coherent areas. Doing so can help different coherent areas to be separated safely to restore stability. In this paper, a frequency-based coherent area boundary identification method has been proposed. This method has been developed relying on the observation of the frequency difference between buses by phasor measurement units deployed by Wide Area Measurement System (WAMS). The proposed method can be used for preliminary or complementary transient stability limit prediction and has been tested with nine bus and two-area benchmark systems using OPAL-RT real-time simulator in Hypersim environment.

articleTitle: Elevating BLDC Motor Performance with Precision PID Controller Tuning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: This proposal introduces a PID controller designed for the speed regulation of BLDC motors in EV systems. The study begins with a comprehensive exploration of BLDC motor characteristics, emphasizing the critical role of accurate speed control in optimizing vehicle performance, energy efficiency, and safety. The core focus lies on the PID controller, renowned for its simplicity and effectiveness in motor speed regulation. The design involves tuning P-I-D gains, with various tuning methods and metaheuristic techniques considering factors such as motor dynamics and system stability. MATLAB simulations validate the PID controller, demonstrating its capacity for accurate and stable speed control across diverse operating conditions. The controller's effectiveness is further confirmed by showcasing its adaptability to step changes, load disturbances, and varying environmental conditions. In conclusion, the implemented PID controller emerges as a practical solution, contributing to the advancement of electric vehicle propulsion systems and promising superior driving experiences in the future.

articleTitle: Optimal Siting and Sizing of Distributed Generation in Distribution Network Using Point Estimate Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: Radial power distribution networks often suffer from significant losses and voltage dips, prompting the introduction of distributed generations (DGs) to address these issues. This study advocates for an optimal arrangement of DGs within distribution networks, encompassing renewable resources like solar power (PV) and windmills (WT), along with conventional sources. Employing the Point Estimate Method (PEM) and evolutionary algorithms, the methodology transforms the framework into a mixed-integer nonlinear problem (MINLP). The effectiveness of this approach is evaluated using a Point Estimate Method (PEM) on an IEEE 69-bus test system. The gathered data reveals the optimal placement and measurements for each DG type. Implementing the suggested solution, which installs DGs according to the Point Estimate Method (PEM), achieves a noteworthy over 2 percent reduction in losses while enhancing voltage levels in distribution networks.

articleTitle: Digital Twin Based Health Monitoring of DC-AC Inverter: A Review
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: This article summarizes the state of digital twin-based health monitoring for DC-AC inverters. When used in conjunction with a real-life DC-AC inverter, a digital twin creates an exact replica of the system in question. It helps keep an eye on the converter and adjust its settings by analyzing readings from the hardware's current sensors. There are a variety of ways to create a digital twin; some are data-driven, while others rely on models. Developing and testing a digital twin approach to DC-AC inverter health monitoring is detailed in this paper. There are two main ways to tell whether a DC-AC inverter is healthy: parameter degradation and fault diagnosis. Data analysis involves comparing sensor readings with data from the digital model in order to determine deterioration characteristics and find defects in the physical system. This presentation will go over several ways to check the DC-AC inverter's health.

articleTitle: A Novel Error Minimization Approach for Real-Time MPPT of Solar PV System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: The solar PV system's performance is greatly affected by environmental uncertainties, making its conversion efficiency very low. Therefore, a novel error minimization approach based on sanitized teacher learning based optimization (s-TLBO) algorithm is proposed for the maximum power point tracking (MPPT) of solar PV system. The real-time setup is developed using 42.13 W polycrystalline solar panel, Arduino UNO, arduino IDE software, digital storage oscilloscope (DSO), and digital multimeter (DMM). The proposed algorithm is employed and tested in real-time and simulation environments, considering varying irradiances. Upon conducting a thorough analysis, it is evident that the proposed algorithm demonstrates reduced settling time, minimized oscillations around the maximum power point (MPP), and decreased overshoot across different solar irradiance levels. Finally, a comparative analysis is performed between the results obtained in real-time and MATLAB environments, revealing a relative difference close to -3.158 %.

articleTitle: Performance Improvement in Droop Controlled Islanded Microgrids via Selective Harmonic Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: The penetration of distributed generation into the grid can be effectively increased with the use of microgrids. Their flexibility to function in both grid-connected and islanded modes enhances the supply reliability for the end user. The manuscript proposes a strategy for improving the quality of load voltage through properly tuned inner controllers in droop controlled islanded microgrids. Traditional droop control allows the inverters to regulate the microgrid's local voltage and frequency independently by sharing the real and reactive power needed by the loads. Instead of using inner controllers, addition of virtual impedance loop is also shown to further improve distortion at the PCC of local load. Further improvement in virtual impedance loop has been shown by adding R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">v</inf> and demonstrated using magnitude and phase plots. The active and reactive power sharing of load, improvement in load voltage distortion have been shown with the help of time domain simulations.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis Between Four-Track EM Launcher and Quadrupole EM Launcher
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of the Quadrupole Electromagnetic Launcher (QEL) using numerical simulations and finite element modeling. The armature body is modeled in ANSYS Electronics, with specifications detailed for materials and dimensions. The working principle of the QEL involves generating Lorentz force without contact losses, achieved through electromechanical energy conversion in the acceleration coil. The magnetic characteristics of the launcher are analyzed, with comparisons made to a four-track electromagnetic launcher. The QEL demonstrates superior flux density, leading to enhanced Lorentz force generation. Current characteristics analysis shows lower current density than the four-track launcher, indicating reduced heating issues. Design parameters for the QEL are discussed, including turns per layer, winding thickness, coil length, length of the wire, total equivalent resistance, and total equivalent inductance. Simulation results show the QEL's performance, with an armature velocity reaching 0.55 m/sec and a force of 250 N provided by the accelerator belt. The study concludes that the QEL is a promising electromagnetic launcher design, offering improved flux density and reduced heating effects compared to traditional designs.

articleTitle: Electric Vehicle to Grid Reactive Power Control Using CPIC Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: Electricity plays a major role in our day to day lives. One such emerging application is the use of an electric vehicle in place of combustion vehicles. As these vehicles consume energy from the power grid along with alternate energy sources like solar charging stations, the need for improving the power quality also increases. This is mainly due to the ever-growing technology which brought a rapid need of power which is varied drastically compared to past life cycle. This in turn will increase the load on the generation and transmission which causes the voltage sags and a drop in the power factor affecting the quality of power. This can be partially addressed with the help of electric vehicles through proper control of the converters used for vehicle to grid connection. This project aims to understand the V2G operation through the classical PI control [CPIC] strategy along with reactive power support where the simulation and analysis of the work is done through PSCAD software.

articleTitle: Investigation of the Impact of Lightning Strikes on Renewable Farms
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: A lightning strike is a natural phenomenon that occurs suddenly, dependent on weather conditions. It can cause overvoltage in any electrical network, including transmission lines and generating stations. However, the increase in renewable farm penetration in recent years, especially in transmission networks, highlights the need to investigate their impact on these farms during such massive surge events. This is important because the equipment in these farms is costly and typically has less withstand capability than other power system network components. This paper uses an IEEE Standard impulse current waveform from PSCAD to investigate the impact of lightning surges on solar and wind farms when connecting them to an IEEE-9 bus network. Additionally, it discusses existing protective measures for such farms in this regard.

articleTitle: Low-Cost Energy Monitoring of gird Connected Solar Photovoltaic Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: The global shift towards renewable energy sources necessitates efficient monitoring solutions for solar photovoltaic (PV) systems to maximize their performance and sustainability. Traditional monitoring systems often involve high costs and complex setups, posing barriers to widespread adoption, particularly for small-scale installations and research projects. In response to these challenges, this paper proposes a novel, low-cost energy monitoring solution tailored for solar PV systems. The system integrates off-the-shelf components, including a Power Supply Hi-Link 5V, an Espressif EP32-WROOM microcontroller, an RS485 to Serial Converter, and an energy meter, offering a cost-effective alternative to conventional monitoring systems. By connecting to the output of the solar PV inverter, our solution captures real-time energy production data, which is seamlessly transmitted to a controller and stored in the cloud-based platform ThingSpeak for remote monitoring and analysis.

articleTitle: A Soft-Switched Voltage Source Inverter Topology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: Soft-switching is a highly effective technique that enhances the efficiency and power density of power electronic converters. To achieve soft-switching in an inverter, a new approach involves the addition of two additional DC-link switches to the existing voltage source inverter setup. This research paper introduces the idea of achieving soft switching for the entire inverter using only a single hard switch. The study includes a comprehensive analysis of the proposed topology, encompassing loss calculations and parameter design, particularly focusing on steady-state conditions. To validate the proposed concept, a 1 kW single-phase inverter model is simulated using MAT-LAB/Simulink. The results indicate that the proposed topology out performs the conventional H - Bridge configuration in terms of efficiency.

articleTitle: Indirect Current Control in Shunt Active Power Filters: Leveraging Downsampling Empirical Mode Decomposition for Improved Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: The increased efficacy of shunt active power filters (SAPF) in harmonic compensation, attributed to the utilization of fast-switching devices and reduced losses, positions them as the preferred solution over traditional passive filter. This paper presents an innovative methodology to indirect current control for SAPF, employing downsampling empirical mode decomposition (DEMD). By leveraging this novel technique, the research aims to enhance the harmonic compensation capabilities of SAPF within distribution systems. The findings of the study demonstrate that the proposed control strategy significantly improves the efficiency of harmonic compensation without compromising the timely tracking of capacitor voltage references. The incorporation of DEMD in the control methodology contributes to the overall advancement of SAPF technology, ensuring better performance and adaptability in mitigating harmonics in distribution networks. This research highlights the potential of DEMD-based control techniques for optimizing SAPF operation, advancing effective and reliable harmonic compensation in power systems.

articleTitle: DC-DC Dual Input Multiport Converter for DC Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: Nowadays adaption of microgrids are creating a revolutionary change. Microgrids are decentralized. It consists of energy storage system, loads and can integrate with different renewable energy sources. This paper proposes and explain about the multiport converter for dc microgrid applications. It explains about how the renewable energies such as solar power connected for the Dual Input Multi Output (DIMO) converter for the microgrid. Solar power generation depends on the irradiance levels. Every time a photovoltaic system is used, its Maximum electricity Point is altered since the amount of power generated from the panels varies. By tracking the maximum power and minimizing ripples MPPT methods such as Ripple Correlation Control (RCC) is applied. By varying the different parameters, the output results for the different irradiation values at different temperatures, the output voltage of the multiport is observed using the MATLAB simulation.

articleTitle: Power Quality Improvement in Grid-Connected PV System with ANN-Based Control Scheme
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: As the global shift towards renewable energy intensifies, grid-connected solar photovoltaic (PV) systems play a key role in meeting sustainable energy requirements. This research paper investigates improvement in power quality [1] in grid-connected solar photovoltaic systems through the implementation of Perturb and Observe (P&O) Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) Algorithm and Artificial Neural Network (ANN) control methods.
