Basically, this paper presents a novel method for detecting islanding based upon image pattern recognition using Random Forest (RF) classification technique is proposed. Images are utilised to derive the histogram of oriented gradient (HOG) characteristics so as to identify non-islanding as well as islanding events. Hence, the time series signal is obtained and transformed into spectrogram images at the point of common connection. These images are utilised to extract the features using histogram of oriented gradient, which is then utilised as a feature vector input for the RF classifier for training as well as testing. It uses rate of change of negative sequence voltage parameter to derive spectrogram image. The RF classifier's effectiveness is assessed with 5, 10, 20 and 25-fold cross-validations. The results from classification demonstrates that detection of islanding using RF classifier and HOG feature being used for image pattern recognition achieved excellent results with 98.75% accuracy and detection time of 192 ms.

articleTitle: Optimal Charging Schedule Coordination of Electric Vehicles by Using Grey Wolf Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: The growing integration of electric vehicles into power distribution networks necessitates the development of efficient and environmentally friendly charging systems. This study presents the Grey Wolf Optimization Algorithm (GWO) as a novel method for optimizing the charge scheduling EVs. The proposed methodology aims to simultaneously minimize charging costs, reduce active power loss within the system, and minimize load variance. At the IEEE-33 Bus system, the effectiveness of the scheduling method, which was developed using the GWO technique, is evaluated within a specific charge duration. The controlled and uncontrolled charging schedules are compared based on charging cost, active power losses, and load variance at high and low penetration of EVs, taking into account a 24-hour load demand profile. The results demonstrate that the suggested coordinated charging schedule effectively minimizes overall cost and active power losses as compared to the uncoordinated charging approach

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning Models for Solar Power Prediction Using Time Series Weather Data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: Smart Grids preside over traditional power grids due to their efficiency and effectiveness. Smart grid implementation has benefited all components of the power system. These grids usually generate energy from renewable energy resources. However, the stability, reliability, and seamless functioning of the grid are adversely affected by the highly weather-dependent characteristics of renewable energy sources. As a result, accurate energy generation forecasting is an essential requirement for the grid's steady and reliable operation. The forecasting techniques for the quantity of electricity produced by solar power plants are discussed in this study. First, the impact of weather on solar power generation is investigated. Second, a machine learning method for solar panel output power prediction based on weather conditions is proposed. Finally, an ensemble approach utilizing different algorithms for machine learning is utilized to boost the accuracy of the proposed model. For the objective of creating prediction models, we utilized a variety of techniques, including temporal convolutional neural networks, fine trees, support vector machines with different kernel functions, artificial neural networks, and long-short-term memory RNNs. Each model's prediction accuracy has been assessed by comparing and contrasting these different methods. A comparative investigation indicated that the Temporal Convolutional Network-based model trumps the others in terms of efficiency. The proposed ensemble model exceeded the conventional individual models after performance comparison with the standard approaches.

articleTitle: Renewable Energy-Based Electrical Infrastructure in France: A Review
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: France is one of the top-growing countries in the world and has a large amount of energy consumption. Nuclear energy is the major source of electricity production in France. Over the last two decades the contribution of renewable energy resources in electricity production has increased. Solar, wind and hydro are the major source of types of renewable electrical energy. The exponential growth of solar and wind energy over the past decade, contribution of hydroenergy in electricty production and other form renewable electrical energy like bioenergy, tidal energy and geothermal energy are discussed here. Statistical data of power generation capacity and electrical energy consumption, and description of some power plants are presented.

articleTitle: Technological and Socio-Economic Review of Solar Based EV Charging Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: Combining solar photovoltaic (PV) systems carbon-free power generation with the clean-driving capabilities of electric vehicles (EVs) offers an attractive path towards sustainable mobility. This dynamic combination has several benefits, both economically and technically. Greenhouse gas emissions usually associated with petroleum powered cars can be greatly reduced thereby resulting in a cleaner world by directly charging EVs with solar energy. Grid-based EV charging has been the subject of numerous studies, but PV charging has also gained interest, in light of the environmentally friendly transportation, this paper offers a thorough summary of recent developments in PV-EV charging systems and Socio-Economic analysis. Further research work has been explored for charging protocols, control schemes, and power converter topologies for gridtied and standalone/hybrid photovoltaic systems.

articleTitle: Optimizing the Integration of Distributed Generation, Shunt Capacitors, and Electric Vehicle Charging Stations into Radial Distribution Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: Excessive fossil fuel consumption, especially in transportation, remains a global concern. In response to this challenge, electric vehicles have surfaced as a viable remedy, attributed to their longevity and diminished greenhouse gas emissions. However, the rapid proliferation of EVs has introduced new challenges, including increased network power loss, deteriorating voltage profiles, and declining substation power factors. This research paper introduces a novel approach, combining fuzzy multi-objective optimization with African vulture optimization algorithm (AVOA), to study the optimum placement with sizing of distributed generation (DG), shunt capacitors (SC), and electric vehicle charging stations (EVCS) in the radial distribution system (RDS). A thorough comparative analysis is undertaken between the explored two-staged approach for the optimal deployment of DG, SC, and EVCS in RDS and existing literature. The results reveal that the proposed method stands on par with existing techniques, demonstrating its competence in minimizing total line power loss and enhancing voltage profile.

articleTitle: Solar-Powered Prototype for Investigation and Analysis of Environmental and Meteorological Parameters that May Affect Dissolved Oxygen
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: Dissolved Oxygen is the most common parameter that causes fish kill to the aquatic production of the fishermen and fishpond owners. This study investigates and analyzes the factors and parameters that lead to the change of dissolved oxygen. Water quality parameters were included like pH, turbidity, salinity, water temperature and dissolved oxygen as well. Meteorological parameters are also considered in the study such as air temperature, wind speed, air pressure, and precipitation. The gathered data for two months imposes that water temperature, salinity and precipitation affects the dissolved oxygen level and the data gathered was sent to thinkspeak. The sensors are powered by solar panel. When the water temperature reached 35°C, the DO starting to changed that may cause stress for the species in the fishpond. Continuous rain is also not good for the dissolved oxygen during rainy season and once the salinity data have a greater than 15g/L.

articleTitle: A Sustainable approach to Design and Optimize a Solar Powered E2W Charging Station for Manipal University Jaipur
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: India witnessed 34.42 % growth of electric two-wheelers (E2W) in the third quarter of fiscal year 2024. The average solar incidence across the country ranges between 4 - 7 kWh/sq.m/day. Adoption of electric vehicles could foster India's commitment towards sustainability. Rajasthan receives the highest annual radiation energy. The state also has highest numbers of universities. Setting up a E2W charging station on the university campus will increase charging convenience, support research activities and reduce the carbon footprint. This case study constructs a self-financed 18.00kWp E2W charging station using PV Syst V7.4.3 software. The Ideal scenario projected a payback period of 6.2 years with 15620.00 USD capital investment. The levelized cost of energy (LCOE) of the E2W station is 0.05 USD which is less than the charging rate of public electric vehicle charging station across the state.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Review of Adaptive Control in Solar PV Integrated EV Charging Station
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: Towards sustainable transportation, development of efficient charging infrastructure for electric vehicle (EV) is evolving day by day. Efficient operation of these charging stations mainly relies on appropriate control of the integrated power converter to address the power quality concerns arising from different non-linear loads. Several conventional and adaptive control approach have been in use for controlling solar photovoltaic (SPV) integrated EV charging station. To provide a general framework of these control aspects, this paper includes a thorough review of several control strategies in ensuring optimal performance grid-integrated EVs. The paper tracks the transition from conventional control techniques to adaptive control methodologies, highlighting their impact on EV charging infrastructure. The review categorizes and evaluates diverse control strategies, ranging from traditional approaches to innovative methods for harmonic extraction and grid integration optimization. The insights from this review contribute to an enhanced understanding of cutting-edge control strategies that can help guide future research efforts aimed at strengthening the reliability of SPV integrated EV charging infrastructure.

articleTitle: Inverse Prediction of Unknown Parameters for a Geothermal/Waste Heat Operated Kalina Cycle
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: In this work, an inverse problem pertaining to the estimation of the operational parameters (OPs) in a low-temperature heat source-driven Kalina cycle (KC) is solved. First, a forward model is used to simulate the KC's steady-state response at various temperatures associated with the superheater (T<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Sup</sup>) and absorber (T<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Abs</sup>), as well as at different strong solution concentrations (X<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Ss</sup>). It is observed that the forward analysis yields the same set of OPs for any optimization target when the net exergy flow rate into the KC system remains constant. This implies that the choice of objective function has no bearing on the optimization process as long as the conditional statement of fixed exergy input is satisfied. A dragonfly algorithm-based inverse analysis is then carried out on the KC system. The research is expected to be useful in choosing KC system's OPs from a range of viable options that can satisfy a desired objective.

articleTitle: A Study on Grid-Tied PV System with Peak Shaving Strategy Using PV Syst Software
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: Electricity is essential for daily life, but alternative energy sources like solar power are gaining popularity due to concerns over greenhouse gas emissions and environmental issues. Overuse of fossil fuels increases CO2 emissions, intensifying storms, hurricanes, droughts, and floods. The research presents a PV-SYST modelling device that simulates gridtied and standalone solar power systems, predicting three dispatch strategies: peak shaving, self-consumption maximization, and weak grid support with battery energy storage systems. These systems increase efficiency and reduce electrical energy waste with less CO2 emissions. The aim is to construct and simulate a 24 KW gridtied solar energy system on the VSSUT campus in Burla, Sambalpur, India, using a fixed tilt strategy developed by the PV-SYST 7.3 program. The goal is to build a solar PV system that eliminates load shedding, lowers power prices, and reduces the system's negative environmental effects.

articleTitle: Voltage Control Management in Transactive Energy Considering Electric Vehicle Charging and Discharging
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: This research introduces a new framework for transactive control in distribution networks that takes into account the operational restrictions of the network to coordinate an aggregator of electric vehicles. The proposed framework makes it easier for electric vehicles to take part in regional energy markets by aggregators, without compromising their own preferences or anonymity. In order to fix voltage issues in distribution networks, the adaptability of EVs in charging and discharging is used. To this purpose, a market price to incentivize EVs to contribute to voltage control in the network. Multiple experiments are carried out on the IEEE 5-node test systems to assess the efficiency of the proposed method. The suggested framework is shown to be successful via simulation results and comparison research in terms of delivering high-quality and voltage management, fulfilling the desires of EV owners, and optimizing computational efficiency.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Techniques for Task Offloading in Connected Autonomous Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: Connected Autonomous Vehicles (CAVs) can revolutionize the haulage industry by improving safety, efficiency, and comfort. However, real-time data processing within latency constraints is crucial for autonomous vehicles to perform well. Due to the limited computational resources available in CAVs, it is important to utilize them efficiently. One way to address this challenge is task offloading, which involves delegating computationally intensive tasks to remote servers or edge devices. In this context, a machine learning-based task offloading system is proposed for CAV s' edge computing networks. This system would dynamically determine the optimal offloading decisions regarding the vehicle's context & network conditions. Additionally, the paper provides a critical review and future roadmap for ML-driven task offloading in CAVs' edge computing environments. Finally, future directions for task offloading in the CAV s system are explored to provide valuable insights for researchers seeking to contribute to advancing the task offloading system.

articleTitle: A Cognitive Approach to Generate Electrical Energy from Acoustic Medium
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: In the modern world, noise has become an omnipresent aspect of daily existence, permeating through urban landscapes, industrial zones, and even natural environments. From the incessant hum of traffic to the cacophony of construction sites, noise pollution has become an inescapable facet of contemporary life. However, amidst the challenges it poses, there lies an untapped potential - the conversion of this acoustic disturbance into a valuable resource: electrical energy. It envisions a future where noise pollution is not merely a nuisance but a valuable asset, paving the way towards a cleaner, greener, and more inclusive energy landscape. In this proposal, the utilization of random sound energy is suggested as an innovative renewable energy source capable of conveniently generating electrical power. The noise (sound energy) produced in the industry by the industrial machinery and noise near traffic junctions is given as the input for the proposed transducer and electrical energy which is generated at the end is used to recharge a battery or used to light up street lights after suitable conversion using some converters. This paper presents a cognitive approach to convert noise pollution into a valuable resource for electricity generation. An introduced hardware prototype can capture sound energy and converting it into electrical power through the utilization of piezoelectric material and diaphragm, and explores how sound waves can be effectively transformed into electrical power.

articleTitle: Eco-Friendly EV Charging: Utilizing Grid-Linked Solar Photovoltaic Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: The integration of renewable energy sources into the electric vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure presents an encouraging route to lessen reliance on fossil fuels and greenhouse gas emissions. This study introduces a novel design and implementation of a Grid Integrated Solar Photovoltaic (PV) Powered Electric Vehicle Charging Station, which leverages the abundance and sustainability of solar energy to power EV charging stations. The proposed system architecture combines a high-capacity solar PV array with grid integration capabilities, ensuring a consistent and reliable power supply for EV charging, irrespective of solar irradiance variability. We explore the technical feasibility, economic viability, and environmental benefits of the system through a comprehensive analysis that includes system design considerations, energy yield predictions, grid interaction strategies, and battery storage solutions to enhance system resilience. Comparing the system to traditional grid-powered EV charging stations, an experiment shows how much carbon emissions it can cut., highlighting its contribution to the decarbonization of the transportation sector. Additionally, the economic analysis reveals that the integration of solar PV with smart grid technologies can offer competitive pricing for EV charging services, encouraging wider EV adoption. The study underscores the importance of leveraging renewable energy technologies in developing sustainable EV charging infrastructures, offering valuable insights for policymakers, investors, and stakeholders in the renewable energy and transportation sectors. Through its innovative approach, the research paves the way for scalable, sustainable, and efficient EV charging solutions that align with global sustainability goals.

articleTitle: Power Extraction and Energy Management with the X - Y Converter for Wind Energy Powered Wireless Isolated DC Loads
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: Across the globe, there is a concerted effort to advance sustainable development generation (SDG) technologies, particularly those capable of supplying electricity to remote regions. This paper proposes an innovative solution in the form of an isolated wind-generating system (WGS) employing a permanent magnet synchronous generator (PMSG) and an active power management strategy. The primary objective of the control technique is to optimize the utilization of wind energy while maintaining a harmonious distribution of active power among three DC wireless loads. The isolated WGS comprises a wind turbine, PMSG, an uncontrolled three-phase (3Φ) rectifier, an X - Y converter, a four-switch bidirectional converter, a storage battery bank, and various wireless DC loads. Notably, the duty cycle of the X - Y converter is finely tuned to maximize wind power output under diverse operational scenarios. Additionally, a power management system is introduced to enhance the overall performance, involving a continuous assessment of generated wind power against load demand power and the state of charge (SOC) of the battery bank. The control of the four-switch bidirectional converter is meticulously orchestrated to maintain a constant DC voltage at the load terminal. Rigorous simulation data validates the effectiveness of the proposed control methodology for the WGS. The results underscore the system's capability to judiciously distribute optimal wind energy among wireless loads and the storage bank, extracting the maximum power potential from the wind while upholding a stable DC voltage level. This research thus contributes valuable insights into sustainable and efficient energy solutions for remote areas.

articleTitle: Advancements in Electrode Materials for Next-Generation Metal Batteries: A Comprehensive Review
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: The pursuit of multivalent metal resources such as Zn, AI, Mg, Ca, and Na has sparked significant interest due to their abundant reserves, low cost, and promising energy density, leading to extensive research into multivalent secondary batteries (MSBs) as potential successors to lithium batteries. Among these metals, sodium has emerged as a particularly viable alternative due to its abundance on Earth's surface. Consequently, there is a compelling rationale to delve deeper into its potential. This review provides an overview of recent advancements in various electrode materials for the next generation of metal batteries. By presenting a comprehensive examination, this review aims to stimulate further interest in a wide array of available electrode materials for metal-ion batteries and facilitate the design of novel battery materials with enhanced performance.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Decision-Making on Strategies for Maximizing the Utility of Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: Environmental sustainability is one of the sustainable development goals and the invention of electric vehicles marks the beginning of alternatives to fuel-based vehicles. Electric vehicles have penetrated the global market to reduce carbon emissions and create a carbon-neutral community. Though these vehicles are environmentally friendly a large population of people in developing nations are still hesitant to purchase these vehicles as they are expensive. This research work proposes strategies for maximizing the utility of E-vehicles based on the obstructing factors using the multi-criteria decision-making method of the Fuzzy Base criterion method (FBCM). The strategies proposed in this paper are ranked based on the score values obtained using representations by trapezoidal fuzzy numbers. The consistency of the results is compared with other decision-making methods and the results obtained using FBCM were found to be more optimal. In this work, the special focus is made concerning developing nations. This paper also presents the extensive role of multi-criteria decision-making methods in designing optimal solutions to the problems of different dimensions associated with electric vehicles.

articleTitle: Review of Microgrid Energy Management in Smart Grid Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: Integration complexity and intermittency of Distributed energy resources (DERs) raise concerns about grid stability, security, and control of microgrids in various operating modes. MGs sustain reliability due to their ability to quickly restore Distributed Power Systems (DPS). The appropriate strategy for MG control is necessary to ensure efficacy of energy management, and qualitative dependability. Alternatively efficient energy management supports MG's operational planning. Networked- Microgrids(NMG) topology has the potential to diminish the imbalances with large-scale RES in sustainability-orchestrated power networks. Transactive energy management (TEM) is an innovative technique to optimize the performance of MG using market mechanisms. This paper reviews challenges in the MG control framework, the diverse energy resources employed in hybrid systems, contemporary operational strategies, effective Energy Management (EM) and research gaps in smart MG environment. This paper aims to provide deep insights to researchers in MG operation and control area.

articleTitle: Enhancing Grid Resilience: Machine Learning-Based Electrical Fault Detection in Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: Electrical fault detection is one of the most critical aspects of maintaining grid resilience and reducing downtime in power systems. However there is a scarcity of adequet systems to detect these anomalies and therefore this research employs modern tools, including machine learning and data analytics, to develop a system capable of distinguishing between anomalies such as equipment breakdowns or short circuits and normal functioning through the analysis of various electrical parameters. In this study, a dataset consisting of Line Current and Line Voltage of different phases was analyzed by applying feature scaling post which different machine learning algorithms such as Decision Tree, Random Forest, MLP, Logistic Regression, and SVM were used to detect and classify the electrical faults that may occur. From the research it was found that KNN outperformed all the other algorithms and managed to achieve the highest overall accuracy as well as highest class-based accuracies as well.

articleTitle: Optimizing Electricity Distribution Through Neutrosophic Transportation Problem Using Contingency Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: Neutrosophic logic presents a sophisticated framework for addressing not just uncertainty but also indeterminacy and inconsistency, making it pivotal for complex problem-solving where traditional fuzzy logic falls short. By including indeterminacy alongside truth and falsity membership functions, neutrosophic logic offers a more nuanced approach to uncertainty modeling, providing an inclusive tool for applications dealing with vague, incomplete, or contradictory information. This article presents the capability of the neutrosophic transportation problem to handle imprecise information, allowing for more flexible and accurate decision-making in the planning and management of the distribution of electricity to various cities from its power plants. With the help of the center of gravity and score function constructing the crisp values, and finding the least transportation cost by evaluating the contingency mean allocation is analyzed in this new technique. This approach has considered, calculating the initial basic feasible solution and optimizing it to minimize the transportation cost for the considered neutrosophic fuzzy numbers.

articleTitle: Quadruped Robot Locomotion Control Using Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: Controlling quadrupedal robots presents significant challenges due to the complexity of their locomotion. Traditional robot control methods often struggle to control the various movements of these robots. In this study, we apply Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) techniques, specifically the Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) algorithm, to design a flexible and autonomous controller for a quadrupedal robot. This Project uses actor-critic models, with the actor issuing control commands and the critic evaluating their effectiveness. We develop a reward system that encourages stability, energy efficiency, and obstacle avoidance. Our experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of DDPG in addressing quadrupedal robot control challenges, underscoring the potential of DRL methods in enhancing robotic systems for real-world applications.

articleTitle: Evaluating the Effect of Electric Vehicle Charging on the Load Profile of the United Arab Emirates Power Grid System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: The study explores the impact of Electric Vehicle (EV) charging on the power grid system in United Arab Emirates (UAE). Using an uncontrolled mathematical model and incorporating survey data, the research analyzes EV load profiles, considering charging energy, timing, and location. Distinct load profiles for level 1 and level 2 charging stations are identified, emphasizing the role of charging power ratings. Despite challenges related to uncertain driver behavior and evolving regulations, the study anticipates a per capita increase in EV passenger cars, highlighting the necessity for strategic planning. While the existing U AE power system can accommodate up to a 20% EV penetration with level 1 charging stations, challenges arise with level 2 charging stations, potentially causing overloads. Looking ahead to 2030, additional challenges emerge, with a 10% EV penetration using level 1 charging stations exceeding the system margin. The study suggests solutions such as dynamic tariffs and the adoption of Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) technology, recognizing V2G-enabled EV s as dynamic grid resources for stability and efficiency. The findings offer insights for policymakers, utilities, and industry stakeholders as they navigate the evolving landscape of EV adoption in the UAE.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Based Modelling for Degradation Analysis and SOH Estimation of Commercial Lithium-Ion Batteries
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) are widely used in electric vehicles due to their high energy and power efficiency. Accurate SOH estimation is essential to ensure the effectiveness and stability of the Battery Management System (BMS). Traditional methods for evaluating battery characteristics are inaccurate, leading to inaccurate SOH estimates. Recent research examines the ability of deep learning (DL) models to estimate battery states. Long-term cycling experiments were conducted using two types of commercial LIBs cells with different cathode material compositions. The DL models were evaluated using root mean square error, mean squared error, mean absolute error, R2, and maximum error. The experimental findings consistently confirm the advantages of the suggested approach, which includes excellent estimate accuracy and satisfied adaptability to various battery chemistries.

articleTitle: Optimal of PID Controller for Enhanced Performance in an AVR System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: This research rigorously examines the effectiveness of an automatic voltage regulator (AVR) system controlled by a carefully designed PID controller. Precise manual tuning with parameters <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Kp}=1.2261, \text{Ki}=0.2902$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Kd}=0.2836$</tex> achieved optimal voltage control, with particular emphasis on transient response characteristics, including overshoot, rise time, and settling time. The results demonstrate the superior capabilities of our custom PID controller. It not only maintains a minimal overshoot of 0.06093%, but also achieves a fast-settling time of only 0.623713 seconds, outperforming other algorithms studied. In addition, the system exhibits an exceptionally negligible steady state error of 0.000016. These technical achievements confirm the advantages of manual tuning over automated approaches and highlight the unsurpassed capabilities of the PID controller in A VR applications. The results contribute significantly to the discourse on A VR systems.

articleTitle: Optimization of Maximum Power Point Tracking Using Hybrid Differential Evolution Flying Squirrel Search Algorithm Under Partial Shading Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: Solar energy production varies because of the ever-changing sunlight intensity and partial shading conditions. The MPPT is among various methods to improve power production. Its purpose is to control the generated voltage and current so that the voltage and related power values are located on the PV curves of photovoltaic cells. Various algorithms have proved to help in optimizing the maximum power conditions, for example the P&O, INC, DE, and FSSA. Trying to contribute to the efforts, this study presents the development of a hybrid method of the DE algorithm and the FSSA to increase the tracking time of the GMPP. DEFSSA method offered a better performance while maintaining high efficiency with the resulted tracking time of 0.4-0.7 second being compared to 1.8-4 seconds using the FSSA method.

articleTitle: Synergizing Renewable Resources: HOMER-Based Case Study on Optimization of Hybrid Energy Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
abstract: Hybrid systems are becoming more and more appealing and are generating a lot of interest due to their unparalleled pricing and operational flexibility. These systems need time-consuming upstream scaling based on accurate knowledge of the electrical energy generated and stored downstream as well as an in-depth understanding of the renewable energy sources present there. Most of the time, extremely potent software is used to optimize the installation economically. The HOMER software is used for simulating and optimizing hybrid energy systems in this paper. This paper provides full and in-depth research on the optimization, design, and techno-economic profitability of the hybrid energy system (wind, PV, and battery energy storage) that is meant to meet the electrical demands of Lakshadweep, an island situated in South India. The electrification project, with its technical and economic feasibility assessment, has been successful in lowering the high expenses associated with employing renewable energy.

articleTitle: Front Matter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Third International Conference on Power Electronics, Intelligent Control and Energy Systems (ICPEICES)
